# CELPIP Listening — Mock Exam Bank (Volume 1)

Contains 180 authentic exam parts with full passages/transcripts, questions, answer keys, and explanations.

## Exam 1 — Part 1: Meal Delivery Mix-Up

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a phone conversation between a customer and a woman who works in customer service at a meal delivery company.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Good afternoon, Weeknight Kitchen customer care, this is Lucia. How can I help you?
MAN: Hi, um, I got my delivery last night, and two of the meals in the bag aren't the ones I picked.
WOMAN: I'm sorry to hear that. Can I get the name on the account?
MAN: Sure, it's Samir Khoury, on Larkspur Crescent. I normally get five meals a week, but I only ordered three this time because I'm visiting my sister in Kingston for four days later this week.
WOMAN: Okay, got it. So what was in the bag?
MAN: Well, the vegetable lasagna's fine. But instead of the salmon and the chicken stir-fry, I got beef tacos and a shrimp pasta. And the thing is, I'm allergic to shellfish.
WOMAN: Oh no. You didn't eat any of the pasta, did you?
MAN: No, no. I always check the label before I heat anything up. And it's not the delivery itself, you know? The bag showed up right on time, and everything was still cold. It's just what was inside.
WOMAN: Thank goodness you checked. Please don't try it, just throw that pasta out. Let me pull up your order and see what our kitchen has on file. Do you mind holding?
MAN: No problem. I'm working from home today, so I'm not going anywhere.

WOMAN: Thanks for holding, Mr. Khoury. Okay, this is a bit strange. The packing list for your order shows the beef tacos, the shrimp pasta and the lasagna. So, um, exactly what you got.
MAN: That can't be right. I picked the salmon and the stir-fry on Sunday night, and I've still got the confirmation email.
WOMAN: Oh, good. Could you forward it to me? That'll really help.
MAN: Sure, I'm sending it now. But can't you just send me the right meals?
WOMAN: Well, here's the tricky part. A replacement gets packed straight from that same list. So if I just pressed resend, you'd get the tacos and the shrimp pasta all over again.
MAN: You're kidding me. Shrimp, twice? I put my allergy on my profile the day I joined, over a year ago!
WOMAN: I know, and I've already put a hold on any replacement. The trouble is, the list gets locked once a bag goes out, so I've sent your email over to the packing team. They work overnight, so they'll see it before morning.
MAN: And what am I supposed to eat in the meantime?
WOMAN: I've refunded the two meals to your card, and I'll call you myself tomorrow morning, once I hear back.
MAN: Fine. I guess it's lasagna tonight, then.

WOMAN: Hi, is this Mr. Khoury? It's Lucia, calling back from Weeknight Kitchen.
MAN: Oh, hi! I wasn't expecting to hear from you this early.
WOMAN: Well, good news. The packing team found the problem. One of your neighbours, a few doors down on Larkspur Crescent, ordered the same night, and when the labels were printed, yours ended up on her bag and hers on yours.
MAN: Huh. So the tacos and the shrimp pasta were hers. She must have ordered the lasagna, too. Do you need the tacos back? I haven't opened them.
WOMAN: No, no, please keep them. She called us this morning, actually, to say she'd got salmon and a stir-fry by mistake. Apparently the salmon was delicious.
MAN: Well, at least somebody enjoyed it.
WOMAN: Your list is fixed now, so a fresh order can go out today. A courier can bring it between six and seven this evening, or it can come with your regular bag next Tuesday.
MAN: Tonight, definitely. I'll be home by half past five.
WOMAN: Great. Just so you know, it won't come in our usual paper bag. It'll be in one of our white cooler boxes, and there'll be a red tag on the lid to show it's been checked for allergies.
MAN: Perfect. Thanks, Lucia. Honestly, I was ready to cancel my account yesterday.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What problem does the man have?
- 1. His bag was delivered later than usual
- 2. His lasagna was missing from the bag
- 3. His bag had meals he did not choose
- 4. His meals were warm when they arrived
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. His bag was delivered later than usual: The man says 'The bag showed up right on time', so the timing was not the problem.
❌ 2. His lasagna was missing from the bag: The lasagna did arrive; he says 'the vegetable lasagna's fine.'
✅ 3. His bag had meals he did not choose: He says 'two of the meals in the bag aren't the ones I picked', and he got beef tacos and a shrimp pasta instead of the salmon and the stir-fry.
❌ 4. His meals were warm when they arrived: He says 'everything was still cold', so the condition of the food was not the issue.

**Q2:** How many meals did the man order this week?
- 1. Two
- 2. Three
- 3. Four
- 4. Five
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Two: Two is the number of meals that were wrong ('two of the meals in the bag'), not the number he ordered.
✅ 2. Three: He says 'I only ordered three this time' because he is visiting his sister.
❌ 3. Four: Four is the number of days he will spend at his sister's in Kingston ('for four days'), not a number of meals.
❌ 4. Five: Five is his usual order ('I normally get five meals a week'), not this week's.

**Q3:** What is true about the man?
- 1. He chose his meals on Saturday night
- 2. He kept proof of the meals he chose
- 3. He added his allergy to his profile recently
- 4. He has already eaten the vegetable lasagna
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. He chose his meals on Saturday night: He says he picked them 'on Sunday night', not Saturday.
✅ 2. He kept proof of the meals he chose: He says 'I've still got the confirmation email', and the woman asks him to forward it.
❌ 3. He added his allergy to his profile recently: He added it 'the day I joined, over a year ago', so it was not recent.
❌ 4. He has already eaten the vegetable lasagna: He says 'I guess it's lasagna tonight', so he has not eaten it yet.

**Q4:** How does the man feel when he hears about the replacement?
- 1. Relieved that he will get his money back
- 2. Worried that he has eaten something unsafe
- 3. Embarrassed that he chose the wrong meals
- 4. Annoyed that the same mistake could happen again
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Relieved that he will get his money back: The refund comes up later, and his reply 'Fine. I guess it's lasagna tonight, then.' sounds resigned, not relieved.
❌ 2. Worried that he has eaten something unsafe: He does not say he ate anything; his complaint is that the shrimp pasta could be sent to him again.
❌ 3. Embarrassed that he chose the wrong meals: He insists 'That can't be right' and says he picked the salmon and the stir-fry, so he does not think the mistake was his.
✅ 4. Annoyed that the same mistake could happen again: When she says 'you'd get the tacos and the shrimp pasta all over again', he answers 'You're kidding me. Shrimp, twice?'

**Q5:** What is most likely true about the woman?
- 1. She will call the man back later tonight
- 2. She works overnight with the packing team
- 3. She needs the packing team to fix the list
- 4. She has already sent the man a replacement
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She will call the man back later tonight: She says 'I'll call you myself tomorrow morning', not tonight.
❌ 2. She works overnight with the packing team: It is the packing team that works overnight ('They work overnight'); she only sends them his email.
✅ 3. She needs the packing team to fix the list: She says 'the list gets locked once a bag goes out, so I've sent your email over to the packing team', which suggests she cannot change the list herself.
❌ 4. She has already sent the man a replacement: She says 'I've already put a hold on any replacement', so nothing has been sent.

**Q6:** Why does the woman call the man?
- 1. To ask him to return the tacos he received
- 2. To explain what caused the problem with his order
- 3. To offer him a refund for the two wrong meals
- 4. To check whether he still plans to cancel
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To ask him to return the tacos he received: The man offers to give the tacos back, and she answers 'No, no, please keep them.'
✅ 2. To explain what caused the problem with his order: She says 'The packing team found the problem' and explains that the labels on his bag and a neighbour's bag were switched.
❌ 3. To offer him a refund for the two wrong meals: The refund was dealt with the day before; she does not mention it in this call.
❌ 4. To check whether he still plans to cancel: He mentions cancelling only at the very end ('I was ready to cancel my account yesterday'), and she never asks about it.

**Q7:** How will the man's new order be packed?
- 1. In a paper bag with a new label
- 2. In a red cooler box with a white tag
- 3. In a white cooler box with a red tag
- 4. In a paper bag with a red tag
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. In a paper bag with a new label: She says 'it won't come in our usual paper bag'.
❌ 2. In a red cooler box with a white tag: The colours are reversed; the box is white and the tag is red.
✅ 3. In a white cooler box with a red tag: She says 'It'll be in one of our white cooler boxes, and there'll be a red tag on the lid'.
❌ 4. In a paper bag with a red tag: The red tag is right, but it goes 'on the lid' of a white cooler box, not on the usual paper bag.

**Q8:** What will most likely happen next?
- 1. The man will cancel his meal delivery account
- 2. The man will receive the right meals tonight
- 3. The neighbour will pass the man's meals along
- 4. The man's meals will come with next week's order
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The man will cancel his meal delivery account: He says he 'was ready to cancel' yesterday, which means he no longer plans to.
✅ 2. The man will receive the right meals tonight: She offers a courier 'between six and seven this evening', and he answers 'Tonight, definitely.'
❌ 3. The neighbour will pass the man's meals along: A fresh order is coming from the company, and the neighbour has already eaten the salmon ('Apparently the salmon was delicious').
❌ 4. The man's meals will come with next week's order: That was the other choice ('with your regular bag next Tuesday'), but he chooses tonight.

## Exam 1 — Part 2: Graphic Design Switch

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a brother and sister. The sister has called her brother on the phone.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Hi, Carlo. Got a minute? I have some news.
MAN: Uh-oh. Sure, I'm out walking the dog. It's minus eight, so talk fast.
WOMAN: Okay. So... I think I'm done with accounting. I want to go into graphic design.
MAN: Rhea, you've been doodling on Mum's grocery lists since you were six. Honestly, what took you so long? No, seriously, what finally pushed you?
WOMAN: The pay's fine, and my supervisor's lovely. It's just six years of the same invoices at the trucking company. The only part I enjoy is designing the charts for our monthly report.
MAN: Ha! That tells you something. So what's the plan?
WOMAN: I took two online courses this summer and loved them. Now I'm looking at a part-time certificate at the college on Portage Avenue. Classes are Tuesday and Thursday evenings for two years, starting in January.
MAN: After a full day at work? That's a lot.
WOMAN: The evenings don't scare me. It's the tuition, about six thousand dollars for the certificate. Part of me wants to quit and do the full-time program. It's only ten months.
MAN: And pay your rent how? Didn't you just renew your lease?
WOMAN: Yeah, yeah, that idea lasted a day. Otherwise I'll wait a year and save up.
MAN: Or ask your company if they help with tuition. Mine paid half of my project management course.
WOMAN: Hmm. It feels kind of weird asking them to pay for me to, you know, leave.
MAN: They don't need your five-year plan. Anyway, do you have to sign up for the whole certificate at once?
WOMAN: No, you can take one course at a time. They're about seven hundred and fifty each.
MAN: Then start with one in January. If you love it, keep going. If not, you've lost a few evenings, not two years.
WOMAN: That's... actually really sensible. Okay, I'll talk to my supervisor on Monday.
MAN: Good. So when can you find out more?
WOMAN: There's an information evening this Thursday, but it's month-end, so I'll be stuck at the office till eight. The next one's Wednesday next week, at seven.
MAN: Go to that one, and call me after with a full report.
WOMAN: Deal. I'll even take notes.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What has the woman called to tell her brother?
- 1. She has signed up for a design certificate that starts in January.
- 2. She is quitting her job to study design full-time.
- 3. She wants to leave accounting for a career in design.
- 4. She has been given a design role at her company.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She has signed up for a design certificate that starts in January: She has not registered. She is only "looking at a part-time certificate," and she still has to go to an information evening to find out more.
❌ 2. She is quitting her job to study design full-time: Quitting was only an idea, and she says "that idea lasted a day."
✅ 3. She wants to leave accounting for a career in design: She opens with "I think I'm done with accounting. I want to go into graphic design."
❌ 4. She has been given a design role at her company: She only designs "the charts for our monthly report," and her job is still "the same invoices at the trucking company."

**Q2:** Why does the woman want to leave her job?
- 1. She feels the pay is too low for her work.
- 2. She is tired of doing the same tasks.
- 3. She does not get along with her supervisor.
- 4. She has to stay late at the office too often.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She feels the pay is too low for her work: She says "The pay's fine," so money is not her reason.
✅ 2. She is tired of doing the same tasks: She describes "six years of the same invoices" and says "The only part I enjoy is designing the charts."
❌ 3. She does not get along with her supervisor: She says "my supervisor's lovely."
❌ 4. She has to stay late at the office too often: She mentions being "stuck at the office till eight" only because this Thursday is month-end, and she never gives late hours as a reason for leaving.

**Q3:** What does the woman's brother suggest she do?
- 1. Wait a year so she can save up
- 2. Quit her job and study full-time instead
- 3. Ask whether her employer helps with fees
- 4. Register for the whole certificate at once
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Wait a year so she can save up: This is the woman's own backup plan, "Otherwise I'll wait a year and save up," not her brother's suggestion.
❌ 2. Quit her job and study full-time instead: This is her idea, and her brother objects with "And pay your rent how?"
✅ 3. Ask whether her employer helps with fees: Her brother says "Or ask your company if they help with tuition."
❌ 4. Register for the whole certificate at once: Her brother asks "do you have to sign up for the whole certificate at once?" and, when she says no, advises "start with one in January."

**Q4:** How does the woman's brother react to her news?
- 1. He thinks the course fees are too high.
- 2. He doubts she has a talent for design.
- 3. He has expected this for a long time.
- 4. He worries that her employer will be unhappy.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. He thinks the course fees are too high: The cost is the woman's worry ("It's the tuition"), and he only suggests ways to handle it.
❌ 2. He doubts she has a talent for design: He says "you've been doodling on Mum's grocery lists since you were six," so he sees her as artistic.
✅ 3. He has expected this for a long time: He recalls her doodling "since you were six" and asks "what took you so long?", so the news is overdue to him, not a surprise.
❌ 4. He worries that her employer will be unhappy: It is the woman who says asking her company "feels kind of weird," and her brother brushes this off with "They don't need your five-year plan."

**Q5:** When will the woman go to the information evening?
- 1. This Thursday evening
- 2. Next Monday evening
- 3. Next Tuesday evening
- 4. Next Wednesday evening
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. This Thursday evening: There is an information evening this Thursday, but she says "it's month-end, so I'll be stuck at the office till eight."
❌ 2. Next Monday evening: Monday is when she will "talk to my supervisor," not when she goes to the college.
❌ 3. Next Tuesday evening: Tuesday is a class night ("Classes are Tuesday and Thursday evenings"), and the classes only start in January.
✅ 4. Next Wednesday evening: She says "The next one's Wednesday next week, at seven," and answers "Deal" when her brother tells her to go to that one.

## Exam 1 — Part 3: Radio Balcony Vegetable Gardening

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation. A radio host is talking with a gardening expert about growing vegetables on an apartment balcony.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Welcome to The Weekend Garden. My guest, Leila Haddad, has spent twenty years at the city greenhouses, raising the flowers you see in our parks. The inbox is full of balcony questions.
WOMAN: No surprise. Just don't ask me about patios. My brother's the landscaper in the family.
MAN: First up is Arjun, who works at a garden centre, so he's a bit embarrassed. He rents a fourth-floor apartment, his balcony faces west, and last summer six tomato plants gave him ten tomatoes. He watered every evening, so he blames shade or wind.
WOMAN: Probably neither. A west balcony gets the six hours of sun tomatoes need, and four floors up isn't that windy. I'd blame his pots, because a five-litre pot is bone dry by mid-afternoon. A tomato plant wants around twenty litres of soil, while herbs are fine with ten.
MAN: That's a lot of pot. Fabric pots or a wooden planter box?
WOMAN: Fabric pots are cheap, light, and fold flat when you move. But they dry out faster, so in a heat wave you'll water twice a day. A sixty-litre wooden box stays moist longer, but it's pricey and weighs a ton when wet.
MAN: Good to know. What about building rules?
WOMAN: Check your lease. Most buildings ban planters hanging outside the railing and water dripping onto the balcony below, so put a tray under every pot.
MAN: Say I'm a total beginner. Where do I start?
WOMAN: Not with a big wooden box full of vegetables. That's for your second summer. Two or three pots of herbs, like basil and parsley, and one cherry tomato. Cherry tomatoes ripen weeks before the big ones, so you get an early reward.
MAN: Confession time. I killed a basil plant last summer.
WOMAN: One basil plant is nothing. On my first balcony I lost every single plant, even the mint, and mint is almost impossible to kill. Twenty years later, the city lets me plant its parks.
MAN: Ha! Could you join our call-in hour next Saturday?
WOMAN: I wish I could, but next Saturday I'm running a free seed swap at the downtown library, ten until two. Bring extra seeds in labelled envelopes, and I'll have a table for balcony questions. The Saturday after, I'm giving tours at the greenhouse open house.
MAN: Two busy Saturdays! Leila Haddad, thank you.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What does the woman do for a living?
- 1. She designs yards for homeowners.
- 2. She grows plants for city parks.
- 3. She sells plants at a garden centre.
- 4. She hosts a gardening show on the radio.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She designs yards for homeowners: That is her brother's line of work; she says 'my brother's the landscaper in the family.'
✅ 2. She grows plants for city parks: The host says she 'has spent twenty years at the city greenhouses, raising the flowers you see in our parks,' and she adds that 'the city lets me plant its parks.'
❌ 3. She sells plants at a garden centre: It is Arjun, the listener, who 'works at a garden centre.'
❌ 4. She hosts a gardening show on the radio: The man is the host; he introduces her as 'My guest, Leila Haddad.'

**Q2:** Why does the woman think Arjun's tomatoes did poorly?
- 1. His balcony did not get enough sun.
- 2. He did not water them regularly.
- 3. His containers held too little soil.
- 4. The wind on his floor was too strong.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. His balcony did not get enough sun: That is Arjun's own guess ('he blames shade or wind'), and she rules it out: 'A west balcony gets the six hours of sun tomatoes need.'
❌ 2. He did not water them regularly: The host says 'He watered every evening.'
✅ 3. His containers held too little soil: She says 'I'd blame his pots, because a five-litre pot is bone dry by mid-afternoon,' while a tomato plant 'wants around twenty litres of soil.'
❌ 4. The wind on his floor was too strong: Arjun's other guess, which she also rules out: 'four floors up isn't that windy.'

**Q3:** How much soil does a tomato plant need, according to the woman?
- 1. about twenty litres
- 2. about five litres
- 3. about sixty litres
- 4. about ten litres
- **Correct Answer:** Option 1
- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. about twenty litres: She says 'A tomato plant wants around twenty litres of soil.'
❌ 2. about five litres: That is the size of Arjun's pots, which she blames for the problem: 'a five-litre pot is bone dry by mid-afternoon.'
❌ 3. about sixty litres: That is the size of the wooden planter box: 'A sixty-litre wooden box stays moist longer.'
❌ 4. about ten litres: That amount is for herbs, not tomatoes: 'herbs are fine with ten.'

**Q4:** What does the woman say a beginner should start with?
- 1. a big wooden box full of vegetables
- 2. a few herbs and a cherry tomato
- 3. full-size tomatoes in fabric pots
- 4. six tomato plants like Arjun's
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. a big wooden box full of vegetables: She puts this off until later: 'Not with a big wooden box full of vegetables. That's for your second summer.'
✅ 2. a few herbs and a cherry tomato: She suggests 'Two or three pots of herbs, like basil and parsley, and one cherry tomato.'
❌ 3. full-size tomatoes in fabric pots: She prefers cherry tomatoes because they 'ripen weeks before the big ones.'
❌ 4. six tomato plants like Arjun's: That is what Arjun tried, and the six plants gave him only 'ten tomatoes.'

**Q5:** Why does the woman mention her first balcony?
- 1. to show that mint is easier than basil
- 2. to show how long she has worked for the city
- 3. to encourage people who are just starting out
- 4. to warn that herbs need a lot of care
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. to show that mint is easier than basil: She says mint 'is almost impossible to kill' only to show how badly her first try went, not to compare herbs.
❌ 2. to show how long she has worked for the city: 'Twenty years later' contrasts her failed start with her success now; her years of service are not the point.
✅ 3. to encourage people who are just starting out: The host has just admitted he 'killed a basil plant'; she replies 'one basil plant is nothing,' then shows that even she 'lost every single plant' at first and still did well later.
❌ 4. to warn that herbs need a lot of care: She recommends herbs for beginners and says mint 'is almost impossible to kill.'

**Q6:** What will the woman do next Saturday?
- 1. give tours at the greenhouse open house
- 2. take calls on the radio program
- 3. run a seed exchange at the library
- 4. answer questions at a garden centre
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. give tours at the greenhouse open house: That happens 'The Saturday after,' not next Saturday.
❌ 2. take calls on the radio program: She turns down the call-in hour: 'I wish I could, but next Saturday I'm running a free seed swap.'
✅ 3. run a seed exchange at the library: She says 'next Saturday I'm running a free seed swap at the downtown library, ten until two.'
❌ 4. answer questions at a garden centre: Her 'table for balcony questions' is at the library seed swap; the garden centre is where Arjun 'works.'

## Exam 1 — Part 5: Residential Street Speeding

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a discussion among three neighbours. They are deciding how to slow down drivers on their street.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming over, you two. Ayesha, Owen did a little experiment on Tuesday. You need to hear this.
C: Yeah. I sat on my front step from five to six and counted. About forty cars, and lots of them were doing way over forty. That's the limit here.
B: Forty cars? That's when the kids are at the playground! Where are they all coming from?
C: The main road, mostly. They cut through here to skip the lights.
A: That's why I asked you both over. I want to ask the city for speed humps. Their website says we need a petition signed by sixty per cent of the households. There are forty-eight on our street.
C: Wow, she's done her homework. So what happens next?
A: Well, that's the catch. They only review requests once a year, and the next round's about eight months away.
C: Eight months? So the only slow thing on this street is the city.
B: Ha! Pretty much. But Mélanie, I'm not so sure about humps. The ploughs take forever to reach us in winter, and humps would slow them down even more. Plus I leave for work at six. I'd be bouncing over them every morning.
A: Fair enough, but we're talking about kids here.
B: I know, I know. What about lawn signs in the meantime? They're about fifteen dollars each. We could have them up this weekend.
A: Signs are a good start, but people tune them out after a couple of weeks.
B: Maybe. Looking back, I'd have pushed for a crosswalk when they built the playground.
A: Wish someone had. There's also the volunteer idea, a few of us in bright vests at the corner for school drop-off. That's at eight-thirty.
C: I like it in theory, but I work rotating shifts at the warehouse. Some weeks I'm on nights, so I can't commit to regular mornings.
B: He's got a point. Why don't we hold off on volunteers until we hear back from the city? If the humps go through, we might not need them.
A: Okay, fair. Ayesha, you'll order the signs?
B: Tonight. Owen, you're off this weekend, right? Want to help me put them up Saturday?
C: Sure, count me in. So she orders, I hammer. And Mélanie, you're taking the petition door to door?
A: Starting tomorrow evening. And the corner volunteers can wait until the city gets back to us.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What has prompted this discussion?
- 1. a near miss involving a child at the playground
- 2. a neighbour's count of drivers speeding on a shortcut
- 3. a request from the school for parent help at drop-off
- 4. a new, lower speed limit near the playground
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. a near miss involving a child at the playground: No accident or near miss is mentioned. Ayesha only points out that the cars come by 'when the kids are at the playground.'
✅ 2. a neighbour's count of drivers speeding on a shortcut: Owen counted 'about forty cars' between five and six, 'lots of them were doing way over forty,' and they 'cut through here to skip the lights.' Mélanie then says, 'That's why I asked you both over.'
❌ 3. a request from the school for parent help at drop-off: School drop-off comes up only later, when Mélanie suggests neighbours in bright vests at the corner. The school asks for nothing.
❌ 4. a new, lower speed limit near the playground: Owen says forty is 'the limit here' and complains that drivers go 'way over' it. Nobody says the limit has changed.

**Q2:** What does the city need before it will review a request for speed humps?
- 1. a $15 fee from each household
- 2. a petition signed by all 48 households
- 3. a petition with 60 per cent support
- 4. a letter of support from the school
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. a $15 fee from each household: Fifteen dollars is what Ayesha says one lawn sign costs. No fee to the city is mentioned.
❌ 2. a petition signed by all 48 households: Forty-eight is the number of households on the street, not the number of signatures the city needs.
✅ 3. a petition with 60 per cent support: Mélanie says the city's website asks for 'a petition signed by sixty per cent of the households.'
❌ 4. a letter of support from the school: The school comes up only for the eight-thirty drop-off. The city never asks for anything from it.

**Q3:** Why does Owen make a joke about the city?
- 1. to complain that the city wants too many signatures
- 2. to poke fun at how long the city takes
- 3. to hint that the speed limit should be lower
- 4. to grumble about the long lights on the main road
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. to complain that the city wants too many signatures: Owen's answer to the sixty per cent rule is 'she's done her homework,' with no complaint. His joke comes only after Mélanie mentions the wait, and it starts 'Eight months?'
✅ 2. to poke fun at how long the city takes: When Mélanie says the next review round is 'about eight months away,' Owen says the city is 'the only slow thing on this street,' a street full of speeding cars.
❌ 3. to hint that the speed limit should be lower: The joke contrasts the slow city with fast drivers. Nobody suggests changing the forty limit.
❌ 4. to grumble about the long lights on the main road: The lights are what drivers 'skip' by cutting through. Owen's joke is about the city's review, not the traffic lights.

**Q4:** What does Ayesha believe about speed humps?
- 1. they would do little to stop drivers cutting through
- 2. they would delay snow clearing on the street
- 3. they would be the surest way to keep kids safe
- 4. they would be approved within just a few weeks
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. they would do little to stop drivers cutting through: Ayesha expects humps to work. She says, 'If the humps go through, we might not need' the volunteers.
✅ 2. they would delay snow clearing on the street: Ayesha says, 'The ploughs take forever to reach us in winter, and humps would slow them down even more.'
❌ 3. they would be the surest way to keep kids safe: That is closer to Mélanie's view ('we're talking about kids here'). Ayesha is 'not so sure about humps.'
❌ 4. they would be approved within just a few weeks: Mélanie says the next review round is 'about eight months away,' and Ayesha does not disagree.

**Q5:** What would Ayesha have done differently?
- 1. started a petition for humps before the playground opened
- 2. requested a crosswalk when the playground was built
- 3. put up lawn signs as soon as the speeding began
- 4. asked the school to move its drop-off time
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. started a petition for humps before the playground opened: The petition is Mélanie's plan for now. Ayesha never says she wishes she had started one.
✅ 2. requested a crosswalk when the playground was built: Ayesha says, 'Looking back, I'd have pushed for a crosswalk when they built the playground.'
❌ 3. put up lawn signs as soon as the speeding began: Lawn signs are Ayesha's plan for this weekend, not something she regrets missing.
❌ 4. asked the school to move its drop-off time: The eight-thirty drop-off is mentioned only as the time for volunteers at the corner.

**Q6:** Why is Owen hesitant about volunteering at the corner?
- 1. he has to leave for work at six every morning
- 2. his work schedule changes from week to week
- 3. he thinks drivers would soon tune them out
- 4. he is busy putting up signs on Saturday
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. he has to leave for work at six every morning: Ayesha is the one who says, 'I leave for work at six.' Owen's hours rotate.
✅ 2. his work schedule changes from week to week: Owen says he works 'rotating shifts' and 'Some weeks I'm on nights, so I can't commit to regular mornings.'
❌ 3. he thinks drivers would soon tune them out: Mélanie says people 'tune them out' about lawn signs, not volunteers, and Owen likes the corner idea 'in theory.'
❌ 4. he is busy putting up signs on Saturday: Owen gladly agrees to help with the signs on Saturday. Drop-off duty would be on school mornings, and his problem is his shifts.

**Q7:** What does Mélanie agree to do?
- 1. order the lawn signs for the street tonight
- 2. collect signatures from the other households
- 3. check the city's review dates on its website
- 4. set up a volunteer roster for school drop-off
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. order the lawn signs for the street tonight: Ayesha takes that job ('Tonight'), and Owen will help her put the signs up.
✅ 2. collect signatures from the other households: Owen asks, 'Mélanie, you're taking the petition door to door?' and she answers, 'Starting tomorrow evening.'
❌ 3. check the city's review dates on its website: Mélanie has already read the city's website. That is not a next step.
❌ 4. set up a volunteer roster for school drop-off: Mélanie says 'the corner volunteers can wait until the city gets back to us.'

**Q8:** What will most likely happen to the idea of corner volunteers?
- 1. it will start at drop-off next Monday
- 2. it will not be decided for several months
- 3. it will be run by parents from the school
- 4. it will begin as soon as the signs are up
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. it will start at drop-off next Monday: Ayesha suggests they 'hold off on volunteers until we hear back from the city,' and Mélanie agrees.
✅ 2. it will not be decided for several months: The volunteers wait for the city's answer, and the city reviews requests only once a year, with the next round 'about eight months away.'
❌ 3. it will be run by parents from the school: Only the neighbours talk about standing at the corner. Nobody mentions parents or the school taking it over.
❌ 4. it will begin as soon as the signs are up: The signs go up this weekend, but Mélanie says 'the corner volunteers can wait until the city gets back to us.'

## Exam 10 — Part 1: Late Dinner Delivery

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman. The woman works at a food delivery service customer support center, and the man is a customer with a complaint.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi, I'm calling about an order I placed through your delivery app about an hour ago. There seems to be a problem with my delivery.
WOMAN: I apologize for any inconvenience. Could you please provide your order number?
MAN: Yes, it's ORDER-5789. I ordered from Golden Dragon Restaurant, and the estimated delivery time was 45 minutes, but it's been over an hour now.
WOMAN: I see your order here. Let me check the status... It appears there was a delay due to high demand in your area. The driver is currently picking up your order.
MAN: That's frustrating. The app still shows the original delivery time, with no updates.
WOMAN: I understand your frustration. I'll make sure to add a note about updating delivery times more frequently. Would you like me to contact the driver for a more precise estimate?
MAN: Yes, please. I need to know if I should make other dinner plans.

MAN: Hi, I'm calling back about my order. The food finally arrived, but there's another issue.
WOMAN: I'm sorry to hear that. What seems to be the problem?
MAN: Well, the food is completely cold, and some items are missing from my order. I ordered kung pao chicken, spring rolls, and fried rice, but the spring rolls aren't here.
WOMAN: I sincerely apologize for this experience. I can see your complete order here. Would you like me to process a refund for the missing spring rolls?
MAN: Well, honestly, the cold food is a bigger issue. Everything's practically inedible.
WOMAN: I completely understand. In this case, I can offer you a full refund for the entire order and add a $10 credit to your account for the inconvenience.
MAN: That would be helpful, thank you.

MAN: Sorry, but I have one more concern before we finish.
WOMAN: Of course, I'm here to help. What's on your mind?
MAN: Well, I noticed the driver didn't follow my delivery instructions. I specifically requested contactless delivery and asked to leave the food at my door, but he kept knocking and waiting.
WOMAN: I apologize for that. I can see your delivery instructions here clearly stated contactless delivery. I'll make sure to report this to our driver support team.
MAN: Thanks. Also, is there any way to ensure I don't get the same driver again? This isn't the first time I've had issues with him.
WOMAN: Yes, I can add a note to your account. In the future, you can also rate drivers through the app, which helps us match customers with preferred drivers.
MAN: Perfect, I appreciate your help with everything today.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the main issue the man initially reports?
- 1. Wrong items in his order
- 2. Delivery time delay
- 3. Payment problem
- 4. Restaurant closure

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Wrong items in his order: The initial complaint wasn't about wrong items.
✅ 2. Delivery time delay: The man's first complaint is that "the estimated delivery time was 45 minutes, but it's been over an hour now."
❌ 3. Payment problem: No payment issues were mentioned in the initial complaint.
❌ 4. Restaurant closure: The restaurant wasn't closed; the order was just delayed.

**Q2:** What does the customer service representative offer to do?

- 2. Give a discount

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Cancel the order: The order was already delivered, so cancellation wasn't offered.
❌ 2. Give a discount: The representative offers credit, not a discount.
✅ 3. Contact the delivery driver: The representative asks "Would you like me to contact the driver for a more precise estimate?" and the customer agrees.
❌ 4. Change the restaurant: This wasn't offered as a solution.

**Q3:** What items did the man order?
- 1. Fried rice and chicken only
- 2. Spring rolls and fried rice only
- 3. Kung pao chicken and spring rolls only
- 4. Kung pao chicken, spring rolls, and fried rice
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Fried rice and chicken only: This is incomplete.
❌ 2. Spring rolls and fried rice only: This is incomplete.
❌ 3. Kung pao chicken and spring rolls only: This is incomplete.
✅ 4. Kung pao chicken, spring rolls, and fried rice: The customer states "I ordered kung pao chicken, spring rolls, and fried rice, but the spring rolls aren't here."

**Q4:** What solution does the representative provide?
- 1. A replacement order
- 2. A full refund plus credit
- 3. A partial refund only
- 4. A discount on next order
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. A replacement order: The representative never offers to replace the order with new food.
✅ 2. A full refund plus credit: The representative specifically says "I can offer you a full refund for the entire order and add a $10 credit to your account for the inconvenience."
❌ 3. A partial refund only: The representative offers more than just a partial refund.
❌ 4. A discount on next order: The representative offers immediate credit, not a discount on a future order.

**Q5:** Which problem was more concerning to the customer?
- 1. The missing spring rolls
- 2. The temperature of the food
- 3. The delivery delay
- 4. The delivery driver's attitude
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The missing spring rolls: The customer indicates this wasn't his biggest concern.
✅ 2. The temperature of the food: When offered a refund for the missing spring rolls, the customer says "Well, honestly, the cold food is a bigger issue. Everything's practically inedible."
❌ 3. The delivery delay: While this was the initial complaint, the cold food became more concerning later.
❌ 4. The delivery driver's attitude: While the customer had issues with the driver not following instructions, he explicitly states the cold food was the bigger issue.

**Q6:** What was in the delivery instructions?

- 2. To leave food at the door
- 3. To deliver to the back entrance
- 4. To text before delivery
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To call upon arrival: This wasn't mentioned in the instructions.
✅ 2. To leave food at the door: The customer says "I specifically requested contactless delivery and asked to leave the food at my door."
❌ 3. To deliver to the back entrance: This wasn't mentioned in the instructions.
❌ 4. To text before delivery: This wasn't mentioned in the instructions.

**Q7:** What does the representative suggest the customer can do in the future?
- 1. Request a specific driver
- 2. Rate the delivery service
- 3. Call customer service first
- 4. Write detailed instructions

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Request a specific driver: The representative doesn't suggest requesting a specific driver.
✅ 2. Rate the delivery service: The representative says "In the future, you can also rate drivers through the app, which helps us match customers with preferred drivers."
❌ 3. Call customer service first: This isn't suggested in the conversation.
❌ 4. Write detailed instructions: The customer already had clear instructions that weren't followed, so this wasn't the suggestion.

**Q8:** What can we infer about the customer's history with this driver?
- 1. This was their first interaction
- 2. They had multiple problems before
- 3. They were usually satisfied
- 4. They never met before
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. This was their first interaction: The customer indicates otherwise.
✅ 2. They had multiple problems before: The customer says "This isn't the first time I've had issues with him" which clearly indicates previous problems.

## Exam 10 — Part 2: Dresser Restoration Guidance

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between two people at a local upcycling furniture workshop. The woman is a workshop instructor, and the man is a new participant.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Welcome to Creative Upcycling Workshop! I see you've brought in an old dresser. Have you done any furniture restoration before?

MAN: Thanks! No, this is my first time. I found this dresser by the curb last week, and I thought instead of letting it go to waste, I could try to give it new life. But I'm not sure where to start.

WOMAN: That's a great attitude! And you've picked a good piece to work with. The wood looks solid despite the worn finish. What's your vision for it?

MAN: I was thinking of painting it navy blue for my daughter's room. But these handles are pretty scratched up. Should I replace them?

WOMAN: Actually, those brass handles are vintage and quite valuable! We can clean them up with some metal polish. They'll look amazing against the navy blue. First, though, we need to prep the surface.

MAN: What does that involve exactly?

WOMAN: We'll start by removing the old varnish with sandpaper, then fill any scratches or dents with wood filler. Once that's dry, we'll sand again to get a smooth surface for painting.

MAN: Sounds like a lot of work! I thought we'd just start painting right away.

WOMAN: That's a common misconception! The prep work is crucial for a professional finish. Trust me, it's worth the extra time. Here, let me show you the right way to sand - go with the grain, like this.

MAN: Oh, I see what you mean. The surface already feels smoother. How long have you been teaching these workshops?

WOMAN: About three years now. I started upcycling furniture as a hobby, but it turned into a real passion. Now I restore pieces for clients and teach others how to do it themselves.

MAN: That's inspiring! Do you think I could learn enough to maybe start doing this as a side business?

WOMAN: Absolutely! Many of our regular participants have started selling their pieces at local markets. But first, let's focus on getting this dresser looking beautiful. Ready to start with the wood filler?

MAN: Yes, definitely! I'm excited to see how it turns out. My daughter will be thrilled to have a unique piece in her room.

WOMAN: That's the best part of upcycling - creating something one-of-a-kind while keeping furniture out of landfills. Let's get started!

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the man's main reason for attending the workshop?
- 1. To start a furniture business
- 2. To learn professional restoration techniques
- 3. To renovate a found dresser
- 4. To meet other furniture enthusiasts
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To start a furniture business: While he asks about this possibility later, it wasn't his initial reason for coming.
❌ 2. To learn professional restoration techniques: He wants to restore a specific piece, not learn professional techniques in general.
✅ 3. To renovate a found dresser: He states he found the dresser by the curb and wanted to "give it new life" for his daughter's room.
❌ 4. To meet other furniture enthusiasts: There's no mention of him wanting to meet others with similar interests.

**Q2:** What does the woman suggest about the dresser's handles?
- 1. They need to be replaced immediately
- 2. They can be restored and are worth keeping
- 3. They should be painted navy blue
- 4. They are too damaged to save
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. They need to be replaced immediately: The woman specifically advises against replacing them.
✅ 2. They can be restored and are worth keeping: The woman says "those brass handles are vintage and quite valuable! We can clean them up with some metal polish."
❌ 3. They should be painted navy blue: The woman suggests the handles will look good against navy blue, not that they should be painted this color.
❌ 4. They are too damaged to save: The woman indicates they can be cleaned up with metal polish, not that they're beyond saving.

**Q3:** What surprises the man about the restoration process?
- 1. The cost of materials needed
- 2. The color choices available
- 3. The amount of preparation required
- 4. The time needed to complete it
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The cost of materials needed: The man doesn't express surprise about costs in the conversation.
❌ 2. The color choices available: The man already had a color in mind (navy blue) and doesn't show surprise about color options.
✅ 3. The amount of preparation required: The man says "Sounds like a lot of work! I thought we'd just start painting right away," showing he's surprised by the prep work needed.
❌ 4. The time needed to complete it: While time is implied in the prep work, his specific surprise is about the amount of preparation, not the overall time.

**Q4:** How did the woman get into furniture restoration?
- 1. Through formal education
- 2. Through a family business
- 3. Through a previous job
- 4. Through a personal hobby
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Through formal education: No mention of formal education in the conversation.
❌ 2. Through a family business: No mention of family involvement in the conversation.
❌ 3. Through a previous job: No mention of a previous job related to restoration.
✅ 4. Through a personal hobby: The woman explicitly states "I started upcycling furniture as a hobby, but it turned into a real passion."

**Q5:** What is implied about the workshop's participants?

- 2. Most are complete beginners
- 3. They often work in teams
- 4. They must have prior experience

- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. Many become professional restorers: The woman states "Many of our regular participants have started selling their pieces at local markets" implying they move to a professional level.
❌ 2. Most are complete beginners: While the man is a beginner, there's no indication that most participants are beginners.
❌ 3. They often work in teams: There's no mention of teamwork in the conversation.
❌ 4. They must have prior experience: The man has no prior experience, proving this isn't a requirement.

## Exam 10 — Part 3: Restaurant Dietary Accommodations

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions

WOMAN: Hi there! I'm calling about your restaurant's new menu. I saw on social media that you've made some changes, and I have some questions since I'm planning to bring a large group next week.

MAN: Of course! Yes, we've updated our menu to be more inclusive of different dietary needs. What would you like to know?

WOMAN: Well, I have several people in my group with different dietary restrictions. One is celiac, two are vegetarian, and another has a severe nut allergy. Will you be able to accommodate everyone?

MAN: Absolutely! That's actually one of the main reasons we updated our menu. We've clearly marked all items that are gluten-free, and we've expanded our vegetarian options from three to twelve different dishes.

WOMAN: That's wonderful! And what about the nut allergy? How careful are you with cross-contamination?

MAN: We take allergies very seriously. We have a completely separate preparation area for allergy-sensitive dishes, and our staff undergoes regular training on allergy protocols. Could you let us know about the allergy when you make the reservation?

WOMAN: Yes, definitely. I'm also curious about your new seasonal menu items. I heard you're working with local farmers now?

MAN: That's right! We've partnered with five local farms to source fresh, seasonal produce. Right now, we're featuring autumn vegetables like butternut squash, rainbow carrots, and local mushrooms. Our chef creates weekly specials based on what's available.

WOMAN: That sounds delicious! Do you recommend making a reservation in advance for a group of eight?

MAN: Yes, especially if you're planning to come for dinner. We're quite busy with the new menu launch, and for groups with dietary restrictions, it helps us prepare better. We can even pre-arrange some menu options for your group.

WOMAN: Perfect! And I noticed you've added some new desserts as well?

MAN: Yes! We now have gluten-free and vegan dessert options. Our pastry chef has created some amazing alternatives, including a dairy-free chocolate mousse and a gluten-free apple crumble that are getting rave reviews.

WOMAN: That's great news! One last question - do you still offer your prix fixe menu for groups?

MAN: We do, but it's been modified to include more options. Groups can now choose from three different prix fixe menus, including one that's entirely vegetarian. Each person can select their preferences from their chosen menu.

WOMAN: Wonderful! You've really thought of everything. I'll call back tomorrow to make the reservation and discuss the details for my group.

MAN: Excellent! We look forward to having you and your group dine with us.

## Exam 10 — Part 5: Endangered Species Initiative

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three members of a local wildlife conservation committee. They are meeting to discuss a new conservation project for endangered species in their region.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming in today. As you know, we need to finalize our plans for the endangered species protection project. The board wants our proposal by next week.

B: Right, and we've narrowed it down to two main options: either focusing on the mountain lions in the northern forest or the wetland restoration for the endangered frogs.

C: The frog population has declined by 60% in just three years. That's pretty alarming. And the wetland project would benefit multiple species, not just the frogs.

A: True, but the mountain lion population is down to just 15 in our region. If we don't act now, they might disappear completely. Plus, they're apex predators – their presence affects the entire ecosystem.

B: The wetland project would be cheaper, though. We could restore three different sites for the same cost as the mountain lion tracking and protection program.

C: What about community support? The farmers up north aren't exactly fans of the mountain lions. Remember last year's livestock incidents?

A: That's actually why I think we need to focus on them. If we can establish proper corridors and protected areas, we could reduce human-wildlife conflict.

B: We'd need to implement some kind of compensation program for the farmers too. That would eat into our budget.

C: The wetland project might be easier to get public support for. We could involve local schools, create educational programs. Kids love frogs!

A: That's a good point. Public engagement is crucial for long-term success.

B: What if we did a hybrid approach? Start with the wetland restoration since it's cheaper, and use that success to build support for the mountain lion project next year?

C: I like that idea. We could even design the wetlands to include viewing platforms, nature trails. Make it a community asset.

A: And we could use the educational programs to raise awareness about both species. Start laying the groundwork for the mountain lion project.

B: The board might prefer that approach too. Less risky, more immediate visible results.

C: We should probably start with the wetland closest to town. That would give us the most visibility.

A: Agreed. Let's draft the proposal focusing on phase one – the wetland restoration. We can include the mountain lion project as phase two for future consideration.

B: Perfect. I can start working on the budget numbers today. We'll need to factor in the educational components.

C: I'll reach out to the schools and see which teachers might be interested in participating. Maybe we could even set up a citizen science program.

A: Excellent. Let's meet again on Friday to review the draft proposal. Sounds like we've got a solid plan coming together.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the main factor influencing the committee's final decision?

- 2. The cost-effectiveness of the project

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The mountain lions' population decline: While mentioned, this wasn't the deciding factor since they postponed this project.

❌ 2. Benefits to multiple species: C explicitly states "the wetland project would benefit multiple species, not just the frogs."
✅ 3. Potential for tourism revenue: While they mention viewing platforms and nature trails, there is no discussion of tourism revenue as an advantage.

**Q4:** What is suggested about the mountain lion project?

- 2. It will be modified significantly

## Exam 10 — Part 6: Electronic Waste Policy

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a report about electronic waste recycling programs in Canada.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** Dr. Chen supports the current recycling programs because .....
- 1. they have eliminated all electronic waste in landfills.
- 2. they encourage manufacturers to make eco-friendly products.
- 3. they have reduced the cost of electronic devices.
- 4. they have decreased overseas shipping of waste.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. they have eliminated all electronic waste in landfills: The content doesn't claim this. In fact, Rodriguez points out that 60% of e-waste still ends up in landfills.
✅ 2. they encourage manufacturers to make eco-friendly products: The content states "According to Chen, the current system creates a direct incentive for manufacturers to design more environmentally friendly products."
❌ 3. they have reduced the cost of electronic devices: This is not mentioned in the content.
❌ 4. they have decreased overseas shipping of waste: The content doesn't mention Chen making this claim.

**Q2:** According to Rodriguez, the main problem with current programs is that they .....
- 1. are too expensive for manufacturers to implement.
- 2. don't address the issue of product durability.
- 3. lack proper collection facilities.
- 4. create unemployment in the recycling sector.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. are too expensive for manufacturers to implement: This is not mentioned as Rodriguez's criticism.
✅ 2. don't address the issue of product durability: The content states Rodriguez argues that "the existing system places too much emphasis on end-of-life recycling rather than addressing the root cause of the problem: excessive consumption and planned obsolescence" and he proposes "strict regulations on product longevity."
❌ 3. lack proper collection facilities: This is not mentioned as Rodriguez's main criticism.
❌ 4. create unemployment in the recycling sector: The content doesn't mention Rodriguez making this claim. In fact, Chen notes the programs have created green jobs.

**Q3:** The difference between provincial programs shows that .....
- 1. smaller provinces have more effective programs.
- 2. British Columbia has the worst collection rates.
- 3. some regions perform better than others.
- 4. Ontario has the most successful program.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. smaller provinces have more effective programs: The content doesn't compare program effectiveness based on province size.
❌ 2. British Columbia has the worst collection rates: The opposite is stated - BC has higher collection rates than Ontario.
✅ 3. some regions perform better than others: The content states "While some provinces have achieved modest success with their programs, others lag significantly behind. British Columbia's program, for instance, has higher collection rates than Ontario's."
❌ 4. Ontario has the most successful program: The content indicates that BC's program has higher collection rates than Ontario's.

**Q4:** Dr. Chen opposes stricter regulations because they might .....
- 1. increase the cost of recycling programs.
- 2. reduce consumer participation rates.
- 3. negatively impact the economy.
- 4. make electronic devices more expensive.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. increase the cost of recycling programs: This reason is not mentioned in the content.
❌ 2. reduce consumer participation rates: This is not mentioned as Chen's concern about stricter regulations.
✅ 3. negatively impact the economy: The content states Chen argues that "a more aggressive regulatory approach could drive manufacturers to relocate their operations outside Canada, potentially leading to job losses and economic disruption."
❌ 4. make electronic devices more expensive: This concern is not attributed to Chen in the content.

**Q5:** Both experts agree that .....
- 1. current programs are completely ineffective.
- 2. public education needs improvement.
- 3. manufacturers should relocate overseas.
- 4. deposit systems are the best solution.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. current programs are completely ineffective: The experts disagree on the effectiveness of current programs. Dr. Chen supports them while Rodriguez criticizes them.
✅ 2. public education needs improvement: The content states "Both experts agree that consumer awareness is crucial" and mentions that surveys show many Canadians are unaware of proper e-waste disposal methods.
❌ 3. manufacturers should relocate overseas: This is not mentioned as a point of agreement. In fact, Dr. Chen warns this could happen with stricter regulations.
❌ 4. deposit systems are the best solution: Only Rodriguez proposes this approach, not both experts.

**Q6:** Recent surveys indicate that many Canadians .....
- 1. prefer to keep their old electronic devices.
- 2. don't support recycling programs.
- 3. lack knowledge about e-waste disposal.
- 4. want stricter environmental regulations.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. prefer to keep their old electronic devices: This is not mentioned in the surveys described in the content.
❌ 2. don't support recycling programs: The content doesn't state this as a survey finding.
✅ 3. lack knowledge about e-waste disposal: The content directly states "Recent surveys indicate that many Canadians are unaware of proper e-waste disposal methods or the environmental impact of electronic waste."
❌ 4. want stricter environmental regulations: This is not mentioned as a finding from the surveys.

## Exam 11 — Part 2: Rooftop Beekeeping Lesson

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between two people at a rooftop urban beekeeping workshop. The woman is an experienced beekeeper, and the man is attending his first workshop.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Welcome to Urban Bees! I'm Sarah, and I'll be leading today's workshop. You seem really excited to be here!

MAN: I am! I'm David. I've been fascinated by beekeeping ever since I saw my neighbor's rooftop hive. I had no idea you could keep bees in the city.

WOMAN: It's becoming quite popular! More people are realizing the importance of bees for urban gardens and food security. Have you had any experience with bees before?

MAN: Not really, just what I've read online. I'm a bit nervous about getting stung, to be honest. Are urban bees different from regular honeybees?

WOMAN: They're the same species, but city bees tend to be quite gentle. We specifically choose docile breeds for urban beekeeping. Here, let me show you how to put on your protective gear properly.

MAN: Thanks! The suit's more comfortable than I expected. So, how many hives do you maintain on this rooftop?

WOMAN: We currently have three colonies, each with about 50,000 bees. Don't worry though – we'll start by observing from a safe distance. See that yellow box over there? That's our newest hive.

MAN: Wow, that's a lot of bees! How do you prevent them from bothering the neighbors?

WOMAN: Good question! We position the hives so the bees fly upward when leaving the hive. Plus, we provide water sources nearby so they don't go searching for water in neighbors' yards.

MAN: That's clever! And how much honey does each hive produce?

WOMAN: In a good season, each hive can produce about 60 pounds of honey. But we always leave enough for the bees to survive winter. Would you like to see inside a hive?

MAN: Really? Is it safe?

WOMAN: Absolutely! We'll use this smoker first – it calms the bees. Then I'll show you how to properly remove a frame. Just remember to move slowly and deliberately.

MAN: This is incredible! I can see why you love doing this. Do you think I could start my own hive?

WOMAN: Definitely! We offer mentoring for new beekeepers. First, though, you'll need to check your local regulations and get permission from your building owner.

MAN: I'll definitely look into that. This workshop is already exceeding my expectations!

## Exam 11 — Part 5: Office Move Logistics

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three employees who work for a technology company. They are meeting to discuss the upcoming office relocation and its implications.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we need to finalize some details about our office move next month. The new building's ready, but there are still some logistics to work out.

B: Yeah, and we really need to figure out the seating arrangements. The new space has an open floor plan, which is quite different from our current setup with individual offices.

C: That's going to be a big adjustment for everyone. I've heard some concerns from my team about noise levels and privacy in an open space environment.

A: Well, we've planned for that. There will be several soundproof meeting rooms and phone booths for private conversations. Plus, we're installing acoustic panels to help with noise reduction.

B: What about the parking situation? I know several employees are worried because the new location is more central, and parking downtown isn't cheap.

A: We're working on that. The building has an underground garage, and we've secured 50 spots. We're also negotiating with a nearby parking lot for additional spaces at a discounted rate.

C: That's good, but what about people who take public transit? The nearest subway station is a 15-minute walk away.

A: Actually, we're planning to provide a shuttle service during peak hours. It'll run between the office and the station every 20 minutes.

B: That's helpful. Now, what about the actual moving process? How are we handling the transfer of equipment and personal items?

A: We've hired a professional moving company. They'll provide packing materials next week, and everyone will need to label their items clearly.

C: And the timeline? We can't afford much downtime with our current projects.

A: The move is scheduled for the weekend. The movers will start Friday evening after everyone leaves, and everything should be set up by Sunday afternoon.

B: What about our clients? Should we inform them about potential disruptions?

C: Good point. We should probably send out a notification, but emphasize that our services won't be interrupted.

A: Exactly. I'll draft a communication plan. We'll also need volunteers from each department to help coordinate their team's move.

B: I can handle that for the development team. We should probably create a detailed checklist for everyone to follow.

C: And maybe we could organize a floor plan tour before the move? It might help people visualize their new workspace and make the transition smoother.

A: Great idea! I'll schedule that for next week. Anything else we need to address?

B: Just one thing - what about the cafeteria setup in the new building?

A: Right, the new space will have a larger break room with better facilities. We're even getting new coffee machines and a proper dining area.

C: That's definitely going to boost morale! Should we plan some kind of office-warming event?

A: Already in the works. We'll have a proper celebration once everyone's settled in.

**Q4:** Both Chen and Rodriguez agree that .....
- 1. all historical buildings should be preserved.
- 2. modern development should take priority.

❌ 4. tourism should drive preservation policies.: While Chen mentions tourism benefits, the content doesn't state both agree tourism should drive preservation policies.

**Q5:** Chen's argument about environmental sustainability suggests that .....
- 1. new buildings are more energy efficient.
- 2. preserving old buildings reduces waste.
- 3. modern construction uses less energy.

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. new buildings are more energy efficient.: Chen actually argues for preservation, not for new buildings being more efficient.
✅ 2. preserving old buildings reduces waste.: The content states Chen argues that "maintaining these buildings is more environmentally sustainable than demolition and new construction, as it reduces waste."

❌ 4. heritage buildings require less maintenance.: The content doesn't mention Chen claiming heritage buildings require less maintenance.

## Exam 12 — Part 1: Concert Ticket Exchange

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman at a concert venue's customer service desk. The woman works at the ticket counter, and the man is a customer.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi there, I bought tickets for tonight's rock concert, but I just found out I can't make it. Is there any way I can exchange them for another date?
WOMAN: I can help you with that. Do you have your tickets with you?
MAN: Yes, here they are. I purchased them online last month.
WOMAN: Let me check the system. The next available show for this band is next Friday. Would that work for you?
MAN: Actually, I'll be out of town next Friday. What about the Saturday show?
WOMAN: Let me see... I'm sorry, but Saturday's show is completely sold out. We do have tickets available for Sunday evening.
MAN: Sunday could work. Would the tickets be in the same section?
WOMAN: Yes, we can get you comparable seats in Section B, Row 15.
MAN: That sounds perfect. What's the exchange fee?
WOMAN: There's a $10 processing fee per ticket for exchanges.

MAN: Before we process the exchange, could you tell me what time the Sunday show starts?
WOMAN: The doors open at 6:30 PM, and the opening act begins at 7:30 PM. The main band usually goes on around 8:45 PM.
MAN: Great, thanks. And is parking included with these tickets like it was with my original ones?
WOMAN: Actually, the Sunday show has different parking arrangements. The main lot will be closed for another event, so concert parking will be in the west garage.
MAN: Oh, I see. Is it far from the venue entrance?
WOMAN: It's about a five-minute walk. We'll have shuttle service running every 15 minutes if you prefer not to walk.
MAN: That's good to know. And will my original parking pass still work?
WOMAN: No, you'll need a new parking pass for the west garage. I can issue that along with your new tickets.

MAN: One more thing - I originally bought three tickets, but only two of us can make it on Sunday. Can I just exchange two tickets and get a refund for the third?
WOMAN: Let me check our policy... I'm afraid we can't issue refunds on individual tickets from a group purchase. You'd need to exchange all three tickets.
MAN: Really? That seems a bit unfair. Is there any way around this?
WOMAN: Well, there is one option. You could exchange all three tickets, and then list the extra ticket on our official resale platform.
MAN: How does that work exactly?
WOMAN: You set your own price, and we list it on our website. When someone buys it, we handle the transaction and transfer the money to your account.
MAN: That sounds like a good solution. Let's do that then.
WOMAN: Perfect. I'll process the exchange and show you how to list the extra ticket.

## Exam 12 — Part 2: Beekeeping Workshop Registration

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a woman who wants to register for a beekeeping workshop and a man who works at a local community center.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Hi there! I saw a flyer about the upcoming beekeeping workshop. Is it still possible to register?

MAN: Yes, absolutely! We still have a few spots available for our weekend workshop. Are you interested in becoming a beekeeper?

WOMAN: I've been thinking about it for a while. My grandfather used to keep bees, and I've always been fascinated. What exactly does the workshop cover?

MAN: It's a comprehensive two-day program. The first day focuses on bee biology, hive management, and basic equipment. The second day is all hands-on experience with actual hives at our community garden.

WOMAN: That sounds perfect! Do I need to bring any special equipment?

MAN: We provide all the protective gear and tools for the workshop. Just wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. Oh, and if you're allergic to bee stings, you'll need to bring your medication, just in case.

WOMAN: I'm not allergic, thankfully. What's the cost of the workshop?

MAN: The workshop is $175, which includes all materials, protective gear rental, and a take-home manual. We also provide lunch both days.

WOMAN: That seems reasonable. When exactly is it happening?

MAN: It's next weekend, Saturday and Sunday, from 9 AM to 4 PM each day. We ask participants to arrive by 8:45 AM for check-in.

WOMAN: Perfect! I'd love to sign up. Do you need any information from me?

MAN: Yes, I'll need your name and emergency contact information. Also, you'll need to sign a liability waiver. Would you like to do that now?

WOMAN: Sure! And is there a deposit required?

MAN: We ask for full payment at registration to secure your spot. We accept credit cards or cash.

WOMAN: I can pay now with my credit card. Oh, one more thing - what if it rains?

MAN: The workshop runs rain or shine! We have an indoor facility for the theoretical portion, and our hives are under covered areas. We'll provide umbrellas if needed.

WOMAN: Wonderful! I'm really excited about this. Let's get me registered then!

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What motivated the woman to take the beekeeping workshop?
- 1. She wants to start a honey business.
- 2. Her grandfather's beekeeping influenced her.
- 3. She saw it advertised on television.
- 4. She needs it for her job.
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. She wants to start a honey business: There is no mention of the woman wanting to start a business.
✅ 2. Her grandfather's beekeeping influenced her: The woman specifically states "My grandfather used to keep bees, and I've always been fascinated."
❌ 3. She saw it advertised on television: She mentions seeing a flyer, not a television advertisement.
❌ 4. She needs it for her job: There is no mention of her job or professional requirements in the conversation.

WOMAN: That sounds exactly like what I'm looking for. What kind of skills would we learn?

MAN: The training covers several essential areas. You'll learn basic disaster response skills like fire safety, light search and rescue, team organization, and disaster medical operations.

WOMAN: Interesting! How long is the training program?

MAN: It's a six-week course, with classes twice a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Each session runs for three hours, from 6:00 to 9:00 in the evening.

WOMAN: That works perfectly with my schedule. Is there any cost involved?

MAN: The program is actually funded by the city, so it's completely free for residents. We just ask for a commitment to complete the full training and be willing to assist during emergencies if needed.

WOMAN: That's very reasonable. Do we need to bring any special equipment?

MAN: The center provides all the necessary training materials and safety equipment. We just ask participants to wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. You might want to bring a notebook and pen for taking notes.

WOMAN: I'd definitely like to secure a spot. Do I need any specific qualifications to join?

WOMAN: That shouldn't be a problem. Will we receive any certification after completing the course?

MAN: Yes, you'll receive an official Community Emergency Response Team certification, which is recognized nationwide. We also provide regular refresher courses every six months to keep your skills sharp.

WOMAN: Perfect! I'd like to sign up. What's the next step?

## Exam 12 — Part 5: Animal Shelter Expansion

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three people who work at a local pet shelter. They are meeting to discuss plans for expanding their facility to accommodate more animals.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming in today. As you know, we're bursting at the seams with our current space, and we need to discuss our expansion options.
B: Yeah, it's getting really crowded. Last week, we had to turn away three families wanting to surrender their pets because we simply didn't have room.
C: And with kitten season approaching, we're going to be in even more trouble. Do we have any concrete plans yet?
A: Well, I've been looking at a few possibilities. The vacant lot next door is for sale, and we could potentially build an extension there. I've got some rough estimates from contractors.
B: That would be ideal location-wise, but what about the cost? Our last fundraiser barely covered our operating expenses for the month.
C: I might have a solution for that. I've been talking to the Mountain View Foundation, and they seem interested in supporting local animal welfare projects. They typically give grants ranging from fifty to a hundred thousand.
A: That's promising! We'd need to put together a solid proposal though. The contractor estimated about eighty thousand for a basic expansion that would give us room for another thirty animals.
B: We should also think about adding some specialized spaces. Like a proper isolation area for sick animals and maybe a larger meet-and-greet room for potential adopters.
C: And what about staff facilities? Right now we're all crammed into that tiny break room.
A: Good points. I can ask the contractor to revise the plans to include those features. Though that would probably push us over a hundred thousand.
B: Maybe we could do it in phases? Start with the basic expansion and add the other features as we secure more funding?
C: That makes sense. We could also reach out to local businesses for sponsorship. You know, name the new wing after them or put up plaques.
A: I like that idea. And we could organize a special fundraising event specifically for the expansion. Something bigger than our usual adoption days.
B: What about a gala dinner? My sister works at the Grand Hotel, and she mentioned they sometimes offer discounted rates for non-profits.
C: A gala would be perfect! We could invite all our regular donors and local business owners. Maybe even have some of our success stories there – you know, adopted pets and their families.
A: This is all coming together nicely. So, let's set some action items: I'll get updated plans from the contractor, Carol can start on the grant proposal, and Brian, you'll look into the gala venue?
B: Sounds good to me.
C: Yes, I'll start working on the proposal right away. Should we meet again next week to review progress?
A: Perfect. Same time next Tuesday? And I'll bring the revised building plans for us to look at.
