## Exam 20 — Part 3: Apartment Maintenance Procedures

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a tenant and a building manager about maintenance and policy updates.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Hi there, I'm from unit 403. I noticed a memo about some changes to the building maintenance schedule and policies.

MAN: Yes, that's right. We're implementing some new procedures starting next month to improve our services. What would you like to know?

WOMAN: Well, first, I saw something about changes to the window cleaning schedule. It used to be quarterly, right?

MAN: Correct. We're actually increasing the frequency to every two months now. Our surveys showed that residents wanted cleaner windows, especially during pollen season and after rain storms.

WOMAN: That's great! And what about the new policy regarding maintenance requests?

MAN: Yes, we're moving to a new online system. Instead of calling the office, residents will need to submit requests through our building's website or mobile app. This helps us track and prioritize requests more efficiently.

WOMAN: I'm not very tech-savvy. Will there still be a way to submit requests in person?

MAN: Of course! We'll keep a paper form system at the front desk for residents who prefer that method. But I encourage you to try the online system - it's very user-friendly, and you can upload photos of any issues.

WOMAN: That's good to know. I also noticed something about changes to the hallway carpet cleaning schedule?

MAN: Yes, we're switching from monthly to bi-weekly carpet cleaning for all common areas. We're also introducing a new spot-cleaning service that will operate daily.

WOMAN: Wonderful! And what about the new garbage disposal rules?

MAN: Right, starting next month, we're implementing mandatory recycling sorting. Each floor will have separate bins for paper, plastic, and general waste. We're also adding a compost bin in the main garbage room.

WOMAN: That makes sense. Will there be any penalties for not following the sorting rules?

MAN: We're starting with a three-month education period where we'll just leave reminder notices. After that, there will be a small fine for repeated violations. We're really trying to make our building more environmentally friendly.

WOMAN: I understand. One last thing - the memo mentioned something about maintenance hours?

MAN: Yes, we've extended our maintenance hours. The team will now be available from 7 AM to 8 PM on weekdays, and we're adding Saturday morning coverage from 8 AM to noon for non-emergency issues.

WOMAN: That's much better than before. Thanks for explaining everything so clearly.

MAN: You're welcome! Don't forget to check your email for the complete policy document. We'll also be hosting an information session next Wednesday in the lobby if you have any other questions.

### Questions & Answer Key

❌ 3. To request window cleaning: She mentions window cleaning as one of the topics but is not requesting the service.
❌ 4. To report a maintenance issue: She doesn't report any issues during the conversation.

- 2. It will be done by a new company
- 3. It will be done more often

- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. It will be done less frequently: The opposite is true - it will be done more frequently.
❌ 2. It will be done by a new company: No mention of changing companies in the conversation.
✅ 3. It will be done more often: The manager states "We're actually increasing the frequency to every two months now" from the previous quarterly schedule.
❌ 4. It will be done on request only: The conversation indicates a regular schedule, not an on-request system.

## Exam 20 — Part 5: Peer Tutoring Launch

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three university staff members who are meeting to coordinate a new peer tutoring service for students. They are discussing how to organize and implement the program.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we're launching the peer tutoring program next semester, and we need to iron out some details. Where should we start?

B: Well, I've been looking at the student survey results, and math and science courses are where students need the most help. Maybe we should focus on those subjects first?

C: That makes sense, but we should also consider writing support. The English department keeps telling me that first-year students really struggle with essay writing.

A: Good points. How many tutors do you think we'll need to recruit?

B: Based on our current enrollment, I'd say at least 20 tutors to start. We can always add more if needed. The challenge will be finding qualified students who can commit to regular hours.

C: Speaking of hours, where are we going to hold these sessions? The library's usually packed, especially during midterms and finals when students need help the most.

A: I've talked to Building Services, and they've agreed to let us use the classrooms in Thompson Hall after 4 PM. They're empty then, and there's plenty of space.

B: That's perfect! But what about compensation? We need to make it worth the tutors' time.

A: The dean approved a budget of $15 per hour for tutors. We can offer them between 5 to 10 hours per week, depending on their schedule and our needs.

C: We should also think about training. We can't just throw them in there without proper preparation.

B: Definitely. I suggest a mandatory two-day training session before the semester starts. We can cover teaching strategies, communication skills, and how to handle different learning styles.

A: Good idea. What about the booking system? Students need an easy way to schedule sessions.

C: I've been looking into some scheduling software. There's one called TutorMatch that looks promising. It lets students book online and sends automatic reminders.

B: Does it track attendance and generate reports? We'll need that data for program evaluation.

C: Yes, it does all that. It's a bit pricey, but I think it's worth the investment.

A: Alright, so let's recap: We'll start with math, science, and writing support, recruit 20 tutors, use Thompson Hall, pay $15 per hour, require training, and use TutorMatch for scheduling. Does that cover everything?

B: We should probably set up regular check-ins with the tutors, maybe monthly meetings to address any issues that come up.

C: And we'll need to promote this service to students. Maybe we can work with the student council to spread the word?

A: Perfect. Let's meet again next week to finalize the training schedule and start the recruitment process.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the primary reason for focusing on math and science first?
- 1. The dean requested these subjects
- 2. Student feedback indicated the need
- 3. These subjects have the highest failure rates
- 4. The tutors prefer these subjects
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The dean requested these subjects: The dean is only mentioned regarding budget approval, not subject selection.
✅ 2. Student feedback indicated the need: B specifically states "I've been looking at the student survey results, and math and science courses are where students need the most help."
❌ 3. These subjects have the highest failure rates: Failure rates are not mentioned in the conversation.
❌ 4. The tutors prefer these subjects: Tutor preferences are not discussed in the conversation.

## Exam 21 — Part 1: Slow Internet Troubleshooting

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi there, I'm here about my internet service. I've been experiencing really slow speeds lately.
WOMAN: I can help you with that. Could I have your account number or address, please?
MAN: Sure, my account number is 45872. I've been a customer for about three years now.
WOMAN: Thank you. I see you're currently on our basic 50 Mbps plan. Have you run any speed tests recently?
MAN: Yes, I did this morning. I'm only getting about 20 Mbps, which is less than half of what I'm paying for.
WOMAN: I understand your frustration. Let me check if there are any reported issues in your area. Hmm... I don't see any network problems. Would you like me to schedule a technician to check your connection?
MAN: Yes, that would be helpful. When's the earliest appointment available?
WOMAN: We have an opening tomorrow morning between 9 and 11, or Friday afternoon between 2 and 4.
MAN: Tomorrow morning works better for me.

WOMAN: While we wait for the technician visit, I noticed you might benefit from upgrading your plan. We're currently offering a special promotion.
MAN: What kind of promotion are you offering?
WOMAN: You can upgrade to our 200 Mbps plan for just $10 more per month, and we'll include free installation and the first month free.
MAN: That sounds interesting. What's the regular price after the promotion ends?
WOMAN: The regular price would be $65 per month, but since you're a loyal customer, I can lock in the promotional rate of $55 for a full year.
MAN: And there are no hidden fees or equipment charges?

MAN: That actually sounds pretty good. But let's wait until after the technician checks my connection before making any changes.

MAN: One more question about the upgrade offer. If I decide to go with it, would I need to sign a long-term contract?
WOMAN: No, we don't require any long-term commitments. You can change or cancel your plan at any time.

WOMAN: The installation typically takes about an hour. The technician coming tomorrow can actually do the upgrade right then if you decide to go ahead with it.
MAN: Perfect. I'll discuss it with the technician after they check my current connection issues.
WOMAN: Sounds good! I've scheduled your appointment for tomorrow between 9 and 11. The technician will call you 30 minutes before arriving.

WOMAN: Those are from our new autumn collection that just arrived. They're not part of the clearance sale, but if you sign up for our loyalty program today, you'll get 15% off your first purchase, including regular-priced items.

## Exam 21 — Part 5: Mental Health Campaign

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three colleagues who work in the Human Resources department. They are meeting to plan a mental health awareness campaign for their company.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we've been tasked with organizing next month's mental health awareness campaign. I think it's crucial we make this impactful.

B: Absolutely. The survey results from last quarter showed that stress levels are pretty high across all departments. We need to address this.

C: I've been doing some research, and I think we should focus on three main areas: stress management, work-life balance, and breaking the stigma around seeking help.

A: Those are great points. What specific activities do you have in mind?

B: Well, I was thinking we could bring in some experts for workshops. I know a certified counselor who specializes in workplace mental health. She's done similar programs at other companies.

C: That's a good start, but we need something more interactive. Maybe we could set up wellness rooms in each department? You know, quiet spaces where people can take short breaks during the day.

A: I like that idea, but we'll need to convince management about the cost-effectiveness. They might worry about productivity.

B: Actually, I have some statistics showing how these wellness initiatives improve productivity in the long run. Companies that implemented similar programs saw a 20% reduction in sick leaves.

C: We should also consider anonymous sharing platforms. Like a board where people can share their experiences or tips anonymously. It might help others feel less alone.

A: That's thoughtful, but we'll need to moderate it carefully. We don't want it to become overwhelming or negative.

B: What about organizing group activities? Like morning meditation sessions or lunchtime walking groups?

C: Yes! And we could create a resource guide. Something simple that lists all the mental health services covered by our insurance, plus helpful apps and websites.

A: These are all excellent suggestions. I think we should spread activities throughout the month rather than cramming everything into one week.

B: Agreed. We could start with the workshops, then gradually introduce the other elements. It'll give people time to adjust and participate in everything.

C: Should we create a schedule now? We could plan which activities go on which days.

A: Good idea. Let's draft something today and then send it to department heads for feedback. We want to make sure it doesn't conflict with any major project deadlines.

B: Perfect. And we should definitely include some form of feedback mechanism to measure the campaign's impact.

A: Absolutely. We'll need that data to justify making some of these changes permanent. Shall we start with the workshop schedule?

WOMAN: That's wonderful! We're always looking for new volunteers. The next orientation session is scheduled for this Saturday at 10 AM.
MAN: Oh, I'm afraid I can't make it this Saturday. I have a family commitment. When's the next available session?
WOMAN: Let me check our calendar... We have another session next Wednesday evening at 6 PM, and then one the following Saturday morning.
MAN: The Wednesday evening session would work perfectly for me. How long does the orientation usually last?
WOMAN: It runs for about two hours. We'll cover all our volunteer programs, safety protocols, and general procedures. You'll also get to meet some of our current volunteers.
MAN: That sounds great. Do I need to bring anything specific with me?
WOMAN: Just bring a government-issued photo ID and something to take notes with. We'll provide all other materials.

MAN: Before I register, could you tell me more about the different volunteer opportunities available?
WOMAN: Of course! We have several programs you can choose from. Our most popular one is the after-school tutoring program for elementary students.
MAN: That sounds interesting. I used to be a math teacher before I retired.
WOMAN: Oh, that's perfect! We're actually short on math tutors right now. We also have a senior companion program, food bank assistance, and our weekend community events team.
MAN: The tutoring program definitely interests me the most. How many hours per week would I need to commit?

WOMAN: Perfect, I've got that down. Oh, and I should mention that we require all volunteers to complete a background check. There's a $20 processing fee for that.

WOMAN: You can pay it at the orientation. We accept cash, credit cards, or checks. And just so you know, once you complete the orientation and background check, you'll need to attend a specific training session for the tutoring program.

## Exam 22 — Part 3: Fine Dining Etiquette

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a restaurant manager and a new employee about dining etiquette.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Welcome to your first day at Le Maison Dorée. Before you start serving customers, I'd like to go over some important dining etiquette rules with you.

MAN: Yes, thank you. I've worked in casual restaurants before, but I know fine dining is quite different.

WOMAN: Indeed, it is. Let's start with the basics. When approaching a table, from which side should you serve the guests?

MAN: I believe it's from the left side, isn't it?

WOMAN: Actually, that's a common misconception. Food is served from the left, but drinks are always served from the right. And when clearing plates, you should also do that from the right side.

MAN: Oh, I see. And what about when guests arrive? What's the proper protocol?

WOMAN: The host should always be greeted within 30 seconds of entering. Pull out chairs for female guests first, then elderly guests, and then others. The host of the party should be seated last.

MAN: Got it. And I noticed there are a lot of different utensils on our place settings. Should I explain these to guests?

WOMAN: Only if they ask. Our guests typically know fine dining etiquette. But remember, utensils are used from the outside in. Salad fork on the outer left, dinner fork inner left, soup spoon outer right, and dinner spoon inner right.

MAN: What about wine service? I'm a bit nervous about that part.

WOMAN: Always present the wine bottle to the host first, showing the label. After approval, serve ladies first, then men, and the host last. Fill glasses only to the halfway point for red wine, and slightly more for white wine.

MAN: And what if I make a mistake or spill something?

WOMAN: Never apologize more than once. If you spill something, say 'I apologize' once, then focus on fixing the situation quickly and efficiently. Get help from other staff if needed, but don't make a scene.

WOMAN: Also, never reach across a guest to serve or clear items. If you can't reach something from the proper side, walk around the table.

MAN: This is all very helpful. What about timing between courses?

WOMAN: There should be a two-minute pause between clearing one course and serving the next. Always ensure all guests at a table are served simultaneously. We have our staff coordinate this in the kitchen.

MAN: And what's the policy on interrupting conversations?

WOMAN: Never interrupt a conversation to serve or clear. Wait for a natural pause. If you need to speak to the table, approach the host and wait to be acknowledged.

MAN: Thank you, this is really comprehensive. I'll make sure to remember all these details.

WOMAN: You'll do fine. Remember, elegance and discretion are our watchwords here. The best service is almost invisible to our guests.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** According to the conversation, what is the correct way to serve at tables?
- 1. Serve everything from the left side
- 2. Serve everything from the right side
- 3. Serve food from left and drinks from right
- 4. Serve based on guest preference
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Serve everything from the left side: This contradicts the information provided.
❌ 2. Serve everything from the right side: This contradicts the information provided.
✅ 3. Serve food from left and drinks from right: The manager explicitly states 'Food is served from the left, but drinks are always served from the right.'
❌ 4. Serve based on guest preference: This is not mentioned in the conversation.

**Q2:** What is the proper seating order for guests?
- 1. Host first, then female guests, then others
- 2. Female guests first, then elderly, host last
- 3. Elderly first, then female guests, host last
- 4. No specific order is mentioned
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Host first, then female guests, then others: This is the opposite of what's stated in the conversation.
✅ 2. Female guests first, then elderly, host last: The manager says 'Pull out chairs for female guests first, then elderly guests, and then others. The host of the party should be seated last.'
❌ 3. Elderly first, then female guests, host last: This contradicts the order specified by the manager.
❌ 4. No specific order is mentioned: A specific order is clearly mentioned in the conversation.

**Q3:** How should servers handle wine service?

- 2. Serve the host first, then others
- 3. Serve men first, then women
- 4. Serve women first, then men, host last
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Fill all glasses completely: The manager says to fill glasses only halfway for red wine and slightly more for white wine.
❌ 2. Serve the host first, then others: The manager states to present the bottle to the host first, but serve them last.

**Q5:** What is the correct timing between courses?

## Exam 22 — Part 5: Fitness Centre Membership Drive

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three employees at a fitness center. They are meeting to discuss strategies for their upcoming membership drive campaign.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming in early, everyone. As you know, our membership numbers have been dropping lately, and we need to come up with some fresh ideas for our spring membership drive.

B: I've been looking at our competitors, and I noticed that most of them are offering really aggressive first-month discounts. Maybe we should consider something similar?

C: The problem with those deep discounts is that people often don't stick around once the regular rates kick in. I think we need something more sustainable.

A: That's a good point. What if we offered a gradual pricing structure? Like, start with a reasonable discount that slowly adjusts to our regular rate over three months?

B: That could work. We could also throw in some extras – maybe three free personal training sessions? It would help new members establish a routine and see real results.

C: I like that idea. When people see results, they're more likely to stay. We could also create some special group fitness challenges for new members. You know, like a six-week transformation program.

A: Speaking of groups, what about a bring-a-friend promotion? Current members could get a discount on their monthly dues if they bring in someone who signs up.

B: That's brilliant! Word of mouth is our best advertising. Plus, people are more likely to stick with their fitness routine if they have a workout buddy.

C: We should also highlight our new equipment. We just invested in those new treadmills and weight machines. That's a major selling point.

A: Definitely. And don't forget about our expanded class schedule. Not many gyms in the area offer both early morning and late evening classes.

B: What about our social media presence? We could showcase some success stories from current members. You know, before-and-after photos, testimonials, that sort of thing.

C: As long as they're willing to share their stories. We could offer them something in return, maybe a free month for being featured?

A: That's reasonable. Now, about the timing – I think we should launch this in April, just when people start thinking about getting in shape for summer.

B: Perfect timing. And we could run it for two months to catch the early summer crowd too.

C: Should we set a target number for new memberships?

A: Let's aim for fifty new members. That's ambitious but achievable. We'll need to have all our staff on board with this campaign.

B: I can start working on the promotional materials right away. We'll need flyers, social media posts, and maybe some local advertising.

A: Excellent. Let's meet again next week to finalize the details and get everyone trained on the new promotion. Thanks for your input, everyone.

MAN: Hi there, I'm wondering if I could book a study room for tomorrow afternoon? I have a group project meeting.
WOMAN: Of course! Let me check the availability. Do you have your student ID card with you?
MAN: Yes, here it is. We'll need the room for about two hours, starting at 2 PM if possible.
WOMAN: Let me see... I'm afraid all our rooms are booked from 2 to 3, but I can offer you a room from 3 to 5 PM. Would that work?
MAN: That might be a bit late. Are there any other options?
WOMAN: Well, we do have Room 204 available from 1:30 to 3:30. How many people will be in your group?
MAN: There will be four of us. Would that room be big enough?
WOMAN: Yes, Room 204 can accommodate up to six people. Would you like me to book that time slot for you?
MAN: Yes, please. That would be perfect.

MAN: Sorry to bother you again, but I have a quick question about the study room facilities.
WOMAN: No problem at all. What would you like to know?
MAN: Does Room 204 have a whiteboard and projector? We'll need to prepare a presentation.
WOMAN: Yes, it has both. There's a large whiteboard on the wall and a ceiling-mounted projector. You'll also find HDMI and VGA cables for laptop connection.
MAN: That's great! And is there Wi-Fi access in the room?
WOMAN: Yes, you can use your student credentials to connect to the university network. There are also power outlets along the walls for your laptops.
MAN: Perfect. One more thing - are we allowed to bring drinks and snacks into the room?
WOMAN: You can bring covered drinks, but food isn't allowed in the study rooms. There's a café on the ground floor if you need refreshments.

MAN: Hi, I'm back. There seems to be a problem with Room 204. We just tried to get in, but our student cards aren't working.
WOMAN: Oh, I apologize for that. Let me check the booking... Ah, I see the issue. The system didn't properly register your booking. Sometimes this happens when we have network issues.
MAN: So what can we do? My group is waiting outside the room.
WOMAN: Let me fix this right away. I'll need to reprocess your booking and reactivate your card access. It should only take a minute.
MAN: That's a relief. We really need to get this presentation done today.
WOMAN: Okay, I've updated it now. Could you tap your card on this reader to verify it's working?
MAN: Yes, the light turned green this time.
WOMAN: Perfect! You should be able to access the room now. Sorry for the inconvenience.

WOMAN: Yes, that's me! Thank you so much. I'm Sarah, and these are scenes from our local hiking trails. I wanted to capture the changing seasons in our community.
MAN: They're incredible! I particularly love this one with the autumn leaves reflecting in the lake. The reds and oranges are so vibrant. How long did it take you to complete this series?

WOMAN: Actually, I do both. I start with quick sketches and color studies on location, then take reference photos. The final pieces are completed in my studio, where I can really take my time with the details.

WOMAN: Yes! In fact, I'm starting to teach a beginner's landscape painting workshop next month. We'll be doing both indoor and outdoor sessions.

WOMAN: I keep the classes small - maximum of eight people - so I can give everyone proper attention. We meet twice a week for six weeks.
MAN: I'd love to sign up. Would it be appropriate for someone with absolutely no painting experience?
WOMAN: Absolutely! That's exactly who the class is designed for. We start with basic techniques and gradually work our way up. By the end, you'll have completed your own landscape painting.
MAN: Wonderful! I'll stop by the front desk to get more information about registration. And congratulations on this beautiful exhibition - you've really captured the spirit of our community.
WOMAN: Thank you! I hope to see you in class next month. Don't forget to sign our guest book on your way out!

## Exam 23 — Part 3: Theme Park Ride Inspections

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a maintenance supervisor and a theme park manager discussing safety regulations.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Good morning, John. I've reviewed the latest safety inspection reports for the rides, and there are a few things we need to discuss before the park opens next week.

MAN: Of course, Sarah. I've been expecting this meeting. What concerns do you have?

WOMAN: Well, first, the Thunder Mountain roller coaster needs immediate attention. The safety harnesses on cars three and five showed signs of wear during the routine check.

MAN: Yes, I noticed that in the report. I've already ordered replacement parts, and they should arrive within two days. We'll have them installed and tested before opening day.

WOMAN: Perfect. Now, about the maintenance schedule - we need to revise it. The current schedule has most rides being inspected on Mondays, but I think we should spread it throughout the week.

MAN: I agree. Having all inspections on one day puts too much pressure on our maintenance team. What's your suggestion?

WOMAN: I'm thinking we should divide the park into zones. Zone A can be Mondays, Zone B on Wednesdays, and Zone C on Fridays. That way, we can ensure thorough inspections without rushing.

MAN: That makes sense. And what about the water rides? They require more frequent checks during peak season.

WOMAN: Yes, those will need daily inspections. I've already assigned two additional staff members to handle the water park area. They'll check water quality, slide surfaces, and safety barriers twice daily.

MAN: Excellent. Have you prepared the new safety announcement schedule for visitors?

WOMAN: Yes, we'll be broadcasting safety messages every hour instead of every two hours. And we've updated the content to include reminders about height requirements and keeping all personal items secured.

MAN: Good thinking. What about the new virtual reality attraction? That needs special attention since it's our first season with it.

WOMAN: Absolutely. I've scheduled additional training for all operators next Tuesday. They need to understand both the technical aspects and the safety protocols. We're also installing new signs explaining the age restrictions and health advisories.

## Exam 23 — Part 5: Holiday Party Venue

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three colleagues who are members of the office social committee. They are meeting to plan the upcoming holiday party for their company.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we need to finalize the details for this year's holiday party. We've got about three weeks left, and there's still a lot to decide.

B: I've been getting a lot of questions from people about the date. Have we settled on that yet?

A: Well, that's actually our first item to discuss. I checked the calendar, and we could do either Friday, December 15th, or Saturday, December 16th.

C: I think we should avoid Saturdays. Last year, attendance was pretty low because people didn't want to give up their weekend. Plus, it was more expensive.

B: I agree. Friday would be better. People are already dressed up for work, and they're in a festive mood. What about the venue?

A: I've narrowed it down to three options. The Grand Hotel downtown, The Riverside Restaurant, or we could do it here in the office like last year.

C: Please, not the office again. It felt too much like we were still at work. People couldn't really relax.

B: The Grand Hotel might be too formal. Remember, we want people to have fun and mingle. What's the Riverside like?

A: They have a private event space with a dance floor, and they're offering a holiday package that includes decorations and a DJ. The menu looks good too.

C: That sounds promising. What about the budget? We have $5,000 to work with, right?

A: Yes, and the Riverside package would be about $3,800, leaving us some money for extras.

B: Like what kind of extras?

A: Well, we could do door prizes, maybe hire a photographer for a couple of hours, or even set up a photo booth.

C: Oh, people loved the photo booth last year! We should definitely do that again.

B: What about food? Is it a sit-down dinner or buffet?

A: It's a buffet with three main course options - chicken, fish, and vegetarian. They'll also have appetizers during the cocktail hour.

C: Perfect. That gives people more chance to mix and mingle instead of being stuck at assigned tables all night.

B: Should we do a theme this year? Something fun like 'Winter Wonderland' or 'Hollywood Glamour'?

A: I like the Winter Wonderland idea. The Riverside already has white and silver decorations in their holiday package.

C: That would work well. We could encourage people to wear blue, silver, or white.

A: Great! So we're settled on Friday the 15th at The Riverside with a Winter Wonderland theme. I'll book it tomorrow and send out the announcements by the end of the week.

B: Sounds like a plan. Should we meet again next week to discuss the smaller details?

A: Yes, let's do that. We still need to plan the timeline for the evening and organize those door prizes.

## Exam 24 — Part 2: Heritage Walking Tour

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a woman who wants to join a local heritage walking tour and a man who works at the community center's information desk.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Hi there! I saw a flyer about the heritage walking tours. Could you tell me more about them?

MAN: Of course! We run guided walking tours every Saturday morning that explore the historical buildings and landmarks in our downtown area. Each tour takes about two hours.

WOMAN: That sounds fascinating! I've lived here for years but never really learned much about the city's history. What time do the tours start?

MAN: The tours begin at 9:30 AM sharp from the steps of the old courthouse. We recommend arriving about 15 minutes early to sign in and meet your guide.

WOMAN: Perfect! And what's the cost for joining?

MAN: It's $15 for adults, which includes a printed guide book with historical photos and information. Seniors and students get a $5 discount.

WOMAN: That's quite reasonable. Do I need to book in advance?

MAN: Yes, we recommend booking at least three days ahead. The tours are limited to 12 people to ensure everyone can hear the guide and ask questions.

WOMAN: I'd like to join this Saturday's tour. Should I be prepared for a lot of walking?

MAN: The route is about two kilometers in total, with several stops along the way. I'd recommend comfortable walking shoes and bringing water, especially on warm days.

WOMAN: And what happens if it rains?

## Exam 24 — Part 3: Renaissance Painting Restoration

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a museum curator and an art restoration specialist.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Good morning, I'm Sarah from the Metropolitan Museum's restoration department. I understand you specialize in historic art restoration techniques?

MAN: Yes, that's right. I've been working in art restoration for over twenty years, focusing particularly on Renaissance-era paintings. What can I help you with today?

WOMAN: We recently acquired a 16th-century painting that needs some careful restoration work. I'm particularly interested in learning about the traditional methods you use.

MAN: Of course. Before we discuss specific techniques, I should mention that I always start with a thorough examination using non-invasive methods. We need to understand the original materials and extent of damage before proceeding.

WOMAN: That makes sense. What kind of examination methods do you typically use?

MAN: I begin with UV light analysis to detect previous restorations and varnish layers. Then I use infrared imaging to see the underlying sketches and changes made by the original artist. These methods help us plan our approach without touching the artwork.

WOMAN: Fascinating! And what about the actual restoration process? I've heard you use some quite traditional materials.

MAN: Indeed. For cleaning, I prefer using natural substances that were available during the period the painting was created. Things like saliva, which contains natural enzymes, or bread dough for gentle cleaning of surface dirt.

WOMAN: Bread dough? That's surprising! I thought that was just an old wives' tale.

MAN: Not at all! It's actually quite effective. The gluten in the dough acts like a gentle eraser. But of course, we also use modern techniques when appropriate. The key is finding the right balance between traditional and contemporary methods.

WOMAN: What about pigments for retouching? Do you create those yourself?

MAN: Yes, I grind many of my own pigments using historical methods. I source minerals and natural materials similar to what the original artists would have used. However, I always ensure these additions are reversible and clearly documented.

WOMAN: That's impressive. How long does a typical restoration project take?

MAN: It varies greatly. A small painting might take three months, while larger works can take over a year. The most time-consuming part is actually the research and testing phase before we even touch the artwork.

WOMAN: Well, this has been incredibly informative. Would you be willing to come to the museum next week to look at our painting and provide a detailed assessment?

MAN: Absolutely. I'd be happy to examine it and provide recommendations. Just remember that with historical pieces, we always aim to preserve rather than perfect. Sometimes the signs of age are part of the artwork's story.

WOMAN: That's exactly the philosophy we're looking for. Thank you for sharing your expertise with us today.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** Why does the woman want to meet with the man?
- 1. To learn about modern restoration techniques
- 2. To discuss a newly acquired painting
- 3. To hire him as a museum curator
- 4. To buy restoration materials
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To learn about modern restoration techniques: She's more interested in traditional methods, not modern ones.
✅ 2. To discuss a newly acquired painting: The woman states, 'We recently acquired a 16th-century painting that needs some careful restoration work.'
❌ 3. To hire him as a museum curator: She's from the restoration department and wants his restoration expertise, not to hire him as a curator.
❌ 4. To buy restoration materials: Purchasing materials is not mentioned in their conversation.

**Q2:** What does the man do before starting restoration work?
- 1. Consults with other experts
- 2. Tests modern cleaning methods
- 3. Conducts non-invasive examinations
- 4. Photographs the artwork
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Consults with other experts: This isn't mentioned in the conversation.
❌ 2. Tests modern cleaning methods: While testing is mentioned, specifically testing modern cleaning methods is not.
✅ 3. Conducts non-invasive examinations: The man states, 'I always start with a thorough examination using non-invasive methods' including UV light analysis and infrared imaging.
❌ 4. Photographs the artwork: Photography isn't mentioned as part of his process.

**Q3:** What surprises the woman during their conversation?
- 1. The use of UV light analysis
- 2. The length of restoration projects
- 3. The use of bread dough for cleaning
- 4. The cost of restoration work
- **Correct Answer:** Option 3
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The use of UV light analysis: The woman doesn't express surprise about this technique.
❌ 2. The length of restoration projects: She doesn't show surprise about the timeframes mentioned.
✅ 3. The use of bread dough for cleaning: The woman explicitly says 'Bread dough? That's surprising! I thought that was just an old wives' tale.'
❌ 4. The cost of restoration work: Cost is not discussed in the conversation.

**Q4:** According to the man, what takes the most time in restoration?
- 1. The actual restoration work
- 2. Creating natural pigments
- 3. Documentation process
- 4. Research and testing phase
- **Correct Answer:** Option 4
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. The actual restoration work: The man specifically states that the research and testing phase takes the most time, not the actual restoration work.
❌ 2. Creating natural pigments: While the man mentions creating pigments, he doesn't indicate this is the most time-consuming part.
❌ 3. Documentation process: Documentation is mentioned but not identified as the most time-consuming aspect.
✅ 4. Research and testing phase: The man explicitly states, 'The most time-consuming part is actually the research and testing phase before we even touch the artwork.'

**Q5:** What is the man's approach to restoration?
- 1. Using only modern techniques
- 2. Combining traditional and modern methods
- 3. Focusing on perfect restoration
- 4. Using only historical methods
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Using only modern techniques: The man doesn't rely solely on modern techniques.
✅ 2. Combining traditional and modern methods: The man explicitly states, 'The key is finding the right balance between traditional and contemporary methods.'
❌ 3. Focusing on perfect restoration: The man actually says the opposite, stating 'we always aim to preserve rather than perfect.'
❌ 4. Using only historical methods: While he uses traditional methods, he also mentions using modern techniques when appropriate.

**Q6:** What is the outcome of their conversation?
- 1. The man agrees to examine the painting
- 2. They schedule regular restoration work
- 3. They decide to use modern techniques only
- 4. The woman decides to look for another specialist
- **Correct Answer:** Option 1
- **Explanation:** ✅ 1. The man agrees to examine the painting: The man responds 'Absolutely. I'd be happy to examine it and provide recommendations' when asked to come to the museum.
❌ 2. They schedule regular restoration work: They only arrange for an initial examination, not regular work.
❌ 3. They decide to use modern techniques only: This contradicts the man's stated approach of balancing traditional and modern methods.
❌ 4. The woman decides to look for another specialist: The woman is satisfied with the man's expertise, saying 'That's exactly the philosophy we're looking for.'

## Exam 24 — Part 5: Internship Program Redesign

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three people who work in different departments at a technology company. They are meeting to discuss changes to the company's internship program.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we need to restructure our internship program. The current system isn't working as well as we'd hoped.

B: I agree. Last summer's interns seemed lost most of the time. We need better organization and clearer goals.

C: And better mentorship. I noticed many interns were just doing basic tasks without real learning opportunities.

A: Exactly. I've drafted some ideas. First, I think we should reduce the number of interns from fifteen to eight. That way, we can provide more focused attention.

B: That makes sense, but won't that affect our recruitment pipeline? HR was counting on converting at least five interns to full-time positions.

C: Quality over quantity, though. I'd rather have eight well-trained interns who really understand our company than fifteen who just make coffee runs.

A: Speaking of training, I suggest we create a structured curriculum. Each intern should rotate through different departments: development, testing, and project management.

B: That's ambitious. We'd need to coordinate with team leaders and ensure they have time to properly train the interns.

C: What about assigning each intern a dedicated mentor? Someone who can guide them throughout the program?

A: Good idea. We could offer incentives to employees who volunteer as mentors. Maybe extra vacation days or professional development credits?

B: I like that. We should also include some practical projects. Last year, the interns complained that they didn't have anything substantial for their portfolios.

C: We could have them work on internal tools. That way, they get real experience, and we benefit from their fresh perspectives.

A: Perfect. And what about the duration? Currently, it's ten weeks. Should we extend it?

B: Twelve weeks might be better. Give them more time to complete their projects and really understand our workflow.

C: If we do that, we should also increase their stipend. The current rate isn't competitive with other tech companies in the area.

A: Agreed. I'll run the numbers and see what we can offer. We also need to think about the interview process. Make it more rigorous.

B: Yes, and maybe include a technical assessment. Something that tests both their skills and problem-solving abilities.

C: And team exercises. We need to make sure they can collaborate effectively.

A: Excellent suggestions. I'll draft a proposal with these changes and send it to leadership next week. We should meet again once we get their feedback.

B: Sounds good. When do we want to implement these changes?

A: Ideally, for next summer's program. That gives us enough time to prepare everything properly.

- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. To save company money: Cost savings are not mentioned as a reason for restructuring.

❌ 4. To meet HR requirements: While HR expectations are mentioned, they're not given as the reason for restructuring.

## Exam 25 — Part 1: Bathroom Ceiling Leak

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman. The woman is a customer service representative at an emergency plumbing company, and the man is a customer with a plumbing issue.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hello, I need emergency plumbing service right away. There's water leaking from my upstairs bathroom ceiling!
WOMAN: I understand this is urgent, sir. Can you tell me your address and contact information?
MAN: Yes, it's 247 Pine Street, and my phone number is 555-0123. My name is David Chen.
WOMAN: Thank you, Mr. Chen. Can you describe what's happening exactly?
MAN: Well, I noticed water dripping from the ceiling below my second-floor bathroom. The spot is getting bigger, and there's a bubble forming in the paint.
WOMAN: Is the water clear or discolored?
MAN: It's brownish, and there's a strange smell.
WOMAN: That sounds like it could be a sewage pipe issue. Have you turned off the main water supply?
MAN: No, I don't know where it is!
WOMAN: It's usually in the basement or near your water meter. I'll guide you through finding it.

MAN: Okay, I'm in the basement now. I see several pipes, but I'm not sure which one is the main.
WOMAN: Look for the largest pipe coming into your house from the street side. There should be a lever or wheel-shaped valve.
MAN: Yes, I found it! It's a red wheel handle.
WOMAN: Perfect. Turn it clockwise until it stops. That should shut off the water supply to your entire house.
MAN: Done. The dripping seems to be slowing down.
WOMAN: Good. I've dispatched our emergency plumber, Mike. He's currently finishing up another job and should be there within the hour.
MAN: An hour? That seems like a long time given the situation.
WOMAN: I understand your concern, but he's actually our closest available technician. In the meantime, place some buckets to catch the water and remove any valuable items from the area.

MAN: The plumber just left, and I wanted to discuss the service charge. The bill seems quite high.
WOMAN: I understand, Mr. Chen. Emergency service, especially during evening hours, does have a higher rate. The invoice shows the standard emergency call-out fee plus three hours of labor.
MAN: But he was only here for two hours!
WOMAN: Let me check the work order... You're absolutely right. I apologize for the error. I'll adjust that right away.
MAN: Thank you. And what about the warranty on the repair?
WOMAN: All our work comes with a 90-day warranty. If you experience any issues related to this repair within that time, we'll fix it at no additional cost.
MAN: That's good to know. Could you email me a copy of the corrected invoice?
WOMAN: Of course. I'll send that to you right away. Is there anything else you need help with?

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the main reason for the customer's call?
- 1. A broken water heater
- 2. A leaking ceiling
- 3. A flooded basement

You will hear a conversation between two people at a local zero-waste living workshop. The woman is a workshop instructor, and the man is a participant who arrived early.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi there! I know I'm quite early, but I wanted to make sure I found the right place. Is this where the zero-waste living workshop is happening?

WOMAN: Yes, you're in the right place! I'm Sarah, the workshop instructor. You're about twenty minutes early, but that's perfect – I could actually use some help setting up the demonstration tables.

MAN: Of course! I'd be happy to help. I'm David, by the way. I've been trying to reduce my waste for a few months now, but I'm finding it pretty challenging, especially with packaging from groceries.

WOMAN: That's actually one of the main topics we'll cover today! I'll show everyone how to shop with reusable produce bags and containers. We've partnered with several local stores that allow customers to bring their own containers for bulk items.

MAN: Really? That would be fantastic! I tried bringing my own containers to a store once, but they wouldn't allow it. Said it was against their policy.

WOMAN: Yes, that's a common issue. We'll provide a list of participating stores in the area. Could you help me arrange these mason jars on the table? We'll use them to demonstrate food storage solutions.

MAN: Sure! These are great – do you actually use all these in your home?

WOMAN: Every single one! They're perfect for storing everything from dried beans to homemade cleaning solutions. Speaking of which, we'll also learn how to make natural cleaning products today.

MAN: That sounds really useful. My kitchen cupboard is full of plastic bottles with different cleaners. It would be great to simplify that.

WOMAN: Exactly! By the end of today's workshop, you'll know how to make all-purpose cleaner, dishwashing liquid, and laundry detergent using just a few basic ingredients.

MAN: I see you also have some fabric items on that table. Are those reusable paper towels?

WOMAN: Good eye! Yes, they're 'unpaper' towels. We'll talk about alternatives to disposable products. I'll demonstrate how to make these, plus beeswax wraps and produce bags.

MAN: This is going to be such an informative session. Oh, look – other people are starting to arrive!

WOMAN: Perfect timing! We've got the tables set up just right. Thanks for your help, David. Find yourself a good seat, and we'll begin in about five minutes!

WOMAN: Of course, I'd be happy to explain our updated policies. We've made several changes to improve our guests' experience. What specific concerns do you have?

MAN: Well, the email mentioned something about new check-in times and cancellation policies. Could you clarify those?

WOMAN: Certainly. Our new check-in time is now 4:00 PM instead of 3:00 PM. This allows our housekeeping team to thoroughly prepare rooms, especially with our enhanced cleaning protocols. Check-out remains at 11:00 AM.

MAN: I see. And what about the cancellation policy? I remember it used to be 24 hours notice.

WOMAN: Yes, that's changed. We now require 48 hours notice for cancellations. If you cancel within that window, there's a one-night charge. However, we've added more flexibility for our reward members – they get 24 hours notice without penalty.

MAN: That's good to know. I noticed something about parking fees changing too?

WOMAN: Yes, we've adjusted our parking rates. Self-parking is now $25 per day, and valet service is $35. However, we've introduced a new weekly rate that offers a 20% discount for stays of 7 days or longer.

MAN: And what about the breakfast service? The email wasn't very clear about that.

WOMAN: We've actually enhanced our breakfast options. Instead of just the traditional buffet, we now offer three choices: the full buffet for $28, a continental breakfast for $18, or an à la carte menu. Room service breakfast is also available from 6:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

MAN: That's helpful. One last thing – I read something about a new resort fee?

WOMAN: Yes, we've implemented a daily resort fee of $30, but it now includes more amenities: Wi-Fi, gym access, pool access, beach towels, and a welcome drink. We've also added complimentary bike rentals and afternoon tea service.

MAN: Well, that doesn't sound too bad. At least we're getting more for the fee.

WOMAN: Exactly. We've tried to add value while keeping our rates competitive. Is there anything else you'd like to know about the new policies?

MAN: No, I think that covers everything. Thanks for explaining it all so clearly.

WOMAN: You're welcome. We look forward to welcoming you tomorrow.

## Exam 25 — Part 5: Industrial Heritage Exhibition

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three members of the local Historical Society. They are meeting to plan their upcoming exhibition about the city's industrial heritage.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming in today. As you know, we need to finalize our plans for the Industrial Heritage Exhibition next month. We've got most things sorted, but there are still some decisions to make.

B: Right, and we need to decide quickly. The posters need to go to print by next week, and we still haven't settled on the exhibition layout.

C: I've been working on the floor plan. I think we should divide it into three main sections: early industrial development, the railway boom, and modern manufacturing. What do you think?

A: That makes sense chronologically. But what about the artifacts from the old textile mill? Mr. Thompson just donated his grandfather's entire collection.

B: Those are incredible pieces! The spinning wheels alone could fill an entire section. Maybe we should rethink the layout to include a special textile corner?

C: Well, we could incorporate them into the early industrial section. The textile industry was crucial to the city's development in the 1850s.

A: Speaking of development, have we confirmed the video presentations? The one about the railway workers' stories is particularly powerful.

B: Yes, I've edited it down to 15 minutes. But we need to decide where to set up the viewing area. It needs to be somewhere dark and quiet.

C: What about using the small room off the main hall? We could set up chairs there, and it would keep the noise contained.

A: Perfect! Now, about the interactive elements – I still think we should let visitors try their hand at some of the old tools.

B: I agree, but we need to consider safety. Maybe we could have supervised demonstrations at specific times?

C: That's a good compromise. We could schedule three demonstrations daily: morning, afternoon, and evening. I can create a roster for volunteers.

A: Excellent. And what about the opening ceremony? The mayor's office confirmed they'll attend.

B: I suggest we start with the traditional ribbon cutting, followed by a guided tour. Then we could have some light refreshments in the courtyard.

C: And don't forget, we need to invite the local press. This is our biggest exhibition of the year.

A: Absolutely. I'll handle the media invitations. So, shall we meet again next Tuesday to review the final layout?

B: Yes, and I'll bring the completed promotional materials for approval.

C: Perfect. I'll have the volunteer schedule ready by then too.

## Exam 26 — Part 1: Houseplant Selection Advice

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a man and a woman at a plant nursery. The woman is a plant specialist, and the man is a customer seeking advice.

### Audio Transcript
MAN: Hi there! I'm looking for some advice about indoor plants. I just moved into a new apartment, and it feels a bit lifeless.
WOMAN: Of course! I'd be happy to help. Do you have any experience with houseplants?
MAN: Actually, no. I've never had plants before, and I'm worried I might kill them. Plus, my apartment doesn't get much natural light.
WOMAN: Don't worry! There are plenty of low-maintenance plants that thrive in low-light conditions. Snake plants and ZZ plants are practically indestructible.
MAN: That sounds promising! But how do I know when to water them? That's what concerns me the most.
WOMAN: These plants are very forgiving. Just check the soil with your finger – if the top inch feels dry, it's time to water. They actually prefer being under-watered rather than over-watered.
MAN: Oh, that's good to know. Could you show me some options?

WOMAN: Here's our low-light plant section. The snake plant is this tall one with the striking pattern.
MAN: I like how it looks, but what about this smaller one with the thick leaves?
WOMAN: That's the ZZ plant I mentioned. It's perfect for beginners and can survive almost anywhere. Would you like to know about care instructions?
MAN: Yes, please. And what size pot should I get? I don't want it to outgrow its space too quickly.
WOMAN: For these plants, I'd recommend a 6-inch pot. They grow slowly, so you won't need to repot for at least a year. Also, make sure to get a pot with drainage holes.
MAN: Great! I'll take both plants. Could you also recommend some potting soil?
WOMAN: Of course! Let me show you our premium indoor potting mix. It has excellent drainage and comes with slow-release fertilizer.

MAN: Hi again! I bought those plants last week, but I'm a bit worried about the snake plant.
WOMAN: What seems to be the problem?
MAN: Well, one of the leaves is turning yellow. I followed your watering advice, but maybe I'm doing something wrong?
WOMAN: Let me take a look at a photo. Ah, I see. Actually, this is normal for older leaves. They naturally yellow and die off as new ones grow.
MAN: Oh, that's a relief! Should I cut it off?
WOMAN: Yes, you can trim it at the base. While you're here, would you like to join our monthly plant care workshop? It's free for customers.
MAN: That would be fantastic! When is it?
WOMAN: We hold them every first Saturday of the month at 10 AM. I can add you to the list right now.

MAN: Yes, absolutely! We're always happy to welcome new photography enthusiasts. I'm David, one of the club organizers.

WOMAN: Great! I'm Sarah. I've been doing photography as a hobby for about a year now, but I'm still learning. I'm not sure if I'm skilled enough to join.

## Exam 26 — Part 3: Marine Conservation Volunteering

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a woman and a man about marine conservation efforts.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Welcome to the Pacific Coast Marine Conservation Center. How can I help you today?

MAN: Hi there! I read about your volunteer program in the local newspaper and I'm really interested in getting involved. I've always been passionate about ocean conservation.

WOMAN: That's wonderful! We're always looking for dedicated volunteers. What aspects of marine conservation interest you the most?

MAN: Well, I'm particularly concerned about the declining sea turtle population. I've been reading about how plastic pollution affects them.

WOMAN: You're absolutely right to be concerned. We actually have several programs focused on sea turtle protection. Our most popular one is the weekend beach cleanup initiative.

MAN: That sounds perfect! What exactly would I be doing as a volunteer?

WOMAN: The beach cleanup runs every Saturday morning from 7 AM to 11 AM. Volunteers work in teams to remove debris from nesting sites and document any turtle tracks or nests they find.

MAN: Do I need any special training or experience?

WOMAN: We provide all necessary training. There's a mandatory three-hour orientation session where you'll learn about local marine species, proper documentation techniques, and safety protocols.

MAN: When's the next orientation session?

WOMAN: We're running one this Thursday evening, and another next Tuesday morning. The evening session starts at 6 PM, and the morning one begins at 9 AM.

MAN: I'll take the Thursday evening session. Is there anything I should bring?

WOMAN: Just bring a notebook and wear comfortable clothes. We'll provide all the materials and equipment you'll need. Oh, and I should mention that we also offer specialized training for those interested in becoming turtle nest monitors.

MAN: That sounds fascinating! What does a nest monitor do?

WOMAN: Nest monitors visit designated beach sections during nesting season to identify and protect new nests. They also help coordinate with our research team to track hatching patterns.

MAN: I'd definitely be interested in that after I get some experience. How long do volunteers usually work before they can become nest monitors?

WOMAN: Most volunteers participate in regular beach cleanups for about three months before moving into nest monitoring. It helps build the necessary observation skills and understanding of turtle behavior.

MAN: Perfect! I'll start with the beach cleanup program and see how it goes. Do I need to sign any forms today?

WOMAN: Yes, we have a basic volunteer agreement and a liability waiver. I can get those for you right now. We're really excited to have you join our conservation efforts!

## Exam 26 — Part 5: Office Relocation Strategy

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three employees who are members of the office relocation committee. They are meeting to discuss plans for moving their company to a new location.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, we need to finalize our office relocation strategy. The lease on our current building expires in four months, so we need to move quickly on this.

B: I've been looking at several potential locations. The one on Westbrook Avenue seems promising. It's a newer building with modern facilities, and it's actually cheaper than what we're paying now.

C: I visited that location last week. While the building is nice, I'm concerned about the parking situation. There are only 50 spots available, and we have 75 employees.

A: That's a valid point. We definitely need adequate parking. What about public transportation options near that location?

B: There's a bus stop about two blocks away, but no subway station within walking distance. I know quite a few of our staff rely on the subway to get to work.

C: What about that building in the downtown area? The one on Marshall Street? It's right next to the central station, so transportation wouldn't be an issue.

A: I looked into that one, but the rent is significantly higher. Plus, we'd need to factor in the cost of renovations to make it suitable for our needs.

B: Speaking of renovations, we should also consider the timeline. How long would it take to get any new space ready? We can't afford to have operations disrupted for too long.

C: Good point. We also need to think about the layout. Our current open-plan office isn't working well for everyone. The development team has been complaining about noise levels affecting their concentration.

A: The Westbrook location actually has a mix of open spaces and private offices. We could potentially create designated quiet zones for the development team.

B: What about meeting rooms? We're constantly struggling to find meeting space in our current location.

C: The downtown building has six meeting rooms of various sizes, while the Westbrook location only has three. But I suppose we could convert some of the private offices into meeting spaces if needed.

A: Let's not forget about the break room and kitchen facilities. Our staff really values having a proper space to eat and socialize.

B: Both locations have decent kitchen facilities, but the downtown space has that nice outdoor patio area that could be great for lunch breaks.

C: True, but remember we're in a climate where outdoor space is only usable for about half the year.

A: Alright, I think we need more information before making a final decision. Could you both prepare detailed reports on these two locations? Include renovation costs, timeline estimates, and potential solutions for the parking and meeting room issues.

B: Sure, I can have that ready by next week.

C: Same here. Should we schedule another meeting for next Thursday to review everything?

A: Perfect. Let's do that. We'll need to make a decision soon to stay on schedule with the move.

### Questions & Answer Key
**Q1:** What is the main challenge facing the committee?
- 1. Finding affordable office space
- 2. Meeting a tight deadline
- 3. Managing renovation costs
- 4. Organizing staff relocation
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. Finding affordable office space: While cost is discussed, it's not presented as the main challenge.
✅ 2. Meeting a tight deadline: A emphasizes 'The lease on our current building expires in four months, so we need to move quickly on this' and later states 'We'll need to make a decision soon to stay on schedule with the move.'
❌ 3. Managing renovation costs: While mentioned, renovation costs are just one factor to consider, not the main challenge.
❌ 4. Organizing staff relocation: The logistics of moving staff is not specifically discussed as a challenge.

**Q2:** What is mentioned as a disadvantage of the Westbrook Avenue location?
- 1. High renovation costs
- 2. Limited parking space
- 3. Poor building condition
- 4. Inadequate kitchen facilities
- **Correct Answer:** Option 2
- **Explanation:** ❌ 1. High renovation costs: Renovation costs are mentioned for the downtown location, not specifically for Westbrook.

MAN: Excuse me, I just arrived on flight AC302 from Vancouver, and my suitcase hasn't shown up on the baggage carousel.
WOMAN: I'm sorry to hear that, sir. May I see your baggage claim ticket and boarding pass?
MAN: Yes, here they are. I've been waiting for over an hour now, and all the other passengers have left with their luggage.
WOMAN: Let me check our system. What color is your suitcase, and are there any distinguishing features?
MAN: It's a dark blue hard-shell suitcase with a bright yellow luggage tag. There's also a small scratch near the handle.
WOMAN: I see. According to our system, your bag was checked in at Vancouver, but... oh, I think I see the issue. It appears your bag was accidentally loaded onto a different flight.
MAN: Oh no! So where exactly is my suitcase now?
WOMAN: Let me check... It was loaded onto flight AC306, which arrives in two hours.

MAN: Two hours? That's quite a wait. Is there anything I can do in the meantime?
WOMAN: Yes, we can take down your contact information and have the bag delivered to your hotel or residence once it arrives.
MAN: That would be helpful. But I have some important medication in that suitcase that I need tonight.
WOMAN: In that case, sir, we can provide you with an overnight essentials kit, and I'll mark your case as urgent.
MAN: What's in the essentials kit?
WOMAN: It includes basic toiletries, a t-shirt, and some other necessities. We can also reimburse you up to $100 for any immediate essential purchases you need to make.
MAN: Well, that's something at least. I'll need to buy some medication though.

WOMAN: Let me see what I can do. I can upgrade your case to priority delivery and have it sent directly to your hotel as soon as it arrives.

MAN: Thank you. And what if the bag doesn't arrive in time for my meeting?
WOMAN: In that case, we would cover reasonable expenses for replacement business attire. Just keep all receipts for reimbursement.

WOMAN: That sounds perfect for us. What other benefits come with the membership?

WOMAN: The guest passes would be perfect when family visits. What about parking? That can add up pretty quickly.

## Exam 27 — Part 3: Digital Nomad Transition

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a woman seeking advice about becoming a digital nomad and a man who is experienced in this lifestyle.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Hi there! I noticed you're working remotely from this café. I've been thinking about becoming a digital nomad myself, and I'd love to get some insights from someone who's actually living that lifestyle.

MAN: Of course! I've been doing this for about three years now. What would you like to know?

WOMAN: Well, I'm currently working as a graphic designer, and I'm wondering how realistic it is to transition to a fully remote lifestyle. What are the main challenges I should be prepared for?

MAN: The biggest challenge is definitely maintaining a stable internet connection. I always research coworking spaces and cafés with reliable WiFi before arriving in a new city. Also, you need to be really organized with time zones when working with clients from different countries.

WOMAN: That makes sense. What about accommodation? Do you book places for long periods, or do you move around frequently?

MAN: I typically stay in each location for at least a month. It's more cost-effective, and you get a better feel for the local culture. Plus, constantly moving can be exhausting and affect your work productivity. I usually book through rental websites that offer monthly discounts.

WOMAN: And what about banking and taxes? That part seems really complicated.

MAN: It definitely can be! I maintain a permanent address in my home country for tax purposes, and I use specific credit cards that don't charge foreign transaction fees. I also keep detailed records of all my expenses and income. Having a good accountant who understands international tax laws is essential.

WOMAN: What about health insurance? That's another concern of mine.

MAN: I have an international health insurance policy that covers me worldwide. It's more expensive than regular insurance, but it's absolutely necessary. You never know what might happen when you're traveling.

WOMAN: Those are all great points. How do you handle the social aspect? Does it get lonely?

MAN: That's actually why I join digital nomad communities in each city I visit. There are lots of online groups where you can connect with other remote workers. I've made some great friends that way. Plus, coworking spaces often organize social events.

WOMAN: That's really helpful! One last question - what's your advice for someone just starting out?

MAN: Start with a trial run. Pick a destination for two or three months and see how you handle working remotely. Make sure you have some savings as a safety net, and try to secure steady clients or remote work before leaving. Also, choose destinations where your money will go further while you're getting established.

WOMAN: Thanks so much for all this advice. It's really helped me get a clearer picture of what to expect.

MAN: No problem! The digital nomad lifestyle can be challenging, but it's incredibly rewarding if you're well-prepared for it.

## Exam 27 — Part 5: Customer Support Improvements

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will watch a discussion among three people who work in the customer service department of a retail company. They are meeting to discuss recent customer feedback and potential improvements.

### Audio Transcript
A: Thanks for coming to this meeting. I've been looking at our customer feedback from the past three months, and there are some issues we need to address.
B: Yeah, I've noticed an increase in complaints lately, especially about our response time. Is that what you're seeing in the data?
A: Exactly. Our average response time has gone from 24 hours to nearly 48 hours. That's not acceptable for our standards.
C: I think part of the problem is that we're understaffed. Since Maria and John left, we've been struggling to keep up with the volume of inquiries.
B: That's true, but I also think we need to look at our processes. I've noticed we're getting a lot of repeat questions that could be addressed with better FAQ sections on our website.
A: Good point. I've compiled some numbers: 40% of our inquiries are about shipping times, 30% about return policies, and 20% about product specifications.
C: Those are exactly the kinds of questions that could be answered automatically. Maybe we should invest in a chatbot for basic inquiries?
B: I'm not sure about that. Remember when our competitor tried that? Their customers hated it.
A: Well, what if we did a hybrid approach? We could have better self-service options but still maintain personal contact for more complex issues.
C: That makes sense. We could also create video tutorials for common problems. I've seen other companies do this successfully.
B: I like that idea. But we still need to address the staffing issue. Even with better self-service options, we need more people.
A: I agree. I've already submitted a request to HR for three new positions. In the meantime, I think we should prioritize our responses better.
C: What do you mean by that?
A: Well, instead of handling everything first-come-first-served, we could categorize inquiries by urgency. Technical issues and order problems would get priority.
B: That could work, but we'd need clear guidelines about what constitutes an urgent issue.
C: And we should make sure customers know about the prioritization system. We don't want them feeling ignored.
A: Absolutely. I'll draft some guidelines and share them with you both by tomorrow. We can implement the new system next week if everyone agrees.
B: Sounds good. Should we also look at extending our service hours?
C: Let's tackle one change at a time. First, let's get the prioritization system working and see how that affects our response times.
A: Agreed. We'll meet again next week to review the guidelines and discuss implementation. Thanks for your input, everyone.

### Questions & Answer Key

MAN: Hi there, I'm looking to book a photographer for my daughter's wedding next spring.
WOMAN: Welcome! I'd be happy to help you explore our wedding photography packages. Do you have a specific date in mind?
MAN: Yes, it's scheduled for May 15th next year. We're expecting about 150 guests.
WOMAN: Perfect timing! Our spring packages are quite popular. We have three main options: Silver, Gold, and Platinum. The Silver package includes 6 hours of coverage, while Gold offers 8 hours, and Platinum provides full-day coverage.
MAN: I see. What's included in the full-day coverage?
WOMAN: The Platinum package covers everything from morning preparations to the evening reception, typically 12 hours. It also includes two photographers, a wedding album, and an engagement photo session.
MAN: That sounds comprehensive, but I'm worried about the cost. What's the price range for these packages?

WOMAN: The Silver package starts at $2,500, Gold is $3,500, and Platinum is $4,800. All packages include edited digital photos and an online gallery.
MAN: That's quite a range. The Platinum package sounds great, but it's over our budget. Could you tell me more about the Gold package?
WOMAN: Of course! The Gold package includes one main photographer and an assistant, 8 hours of coverage, 400 edited photos, a medium-sized wedding album, and a USB drive with all images.
MAN: And what about the engagement session? Is that only with the Platinum package?
WOMAN: The engagement session is included in Platinum, but you can add it to any package for $350. Many couples find it helpful to work with their photographer before the wedding day.
MAN: That makes sense. And what about the deposit requirements?

WOMAN: We require a 30% deposit to secure your date, with the balance due two weeks before the wedding. For the Gold package, that would be about $1,050 initially.
MAN: I need to discuss this with my wife and daughter. Do you have any available dates around May 15th?
WOMAN: Let me check our calendar... We're actually available on May 15th, and also the 14th and 16th. Would you like me to hold any of these dates temporarily?
MAN: Yes, could you please hold May 15th for 48 hours? That would give us time to make a decision.
WOMAN: Absolutely! I'll mark it as pending until Wednesday. Here's our brochure with all the package details, and my business card. Feel free to call if you have any questions.
MAN: Thanks so much for your help. We'll definitely be in touch soon.

MAN: Of course! What can I help you with?

WOMAN: Well, I'm going on vacation next week for 10 days, and I need someone to look after my cat, Mittens. Would you be interested in pet-sitting?

MAN: I'd be happy to help! I love cats, and my dog Max is very friendly with them. What would I need to do?

WOMAN: Mainly just feeding her twice a day, changing her water, and cleaning the litter box. She's very independent but loves attention when she's in the mood.

MAN: That sounds manageable. Does she need any special food or medication?

WOMAN: She's on a special diet for sensitive stomachs. I'll leave detailed instructions and plenty of food. The only tricky part is that she needs to be fed at specific times - 7 AM and 6 PM.

MAN: That works perfectly with Max's walking schedule. Do you have a spare key, or should I use the garage code?

WOMAN: I'll give you the spare key and show you where everything is. Would you like to come over tomorrow to meet Mittens? That way, she'll be familiar with you before I leave.

MAN: That's a great idea! What time works for you?

WOMAN: How about around 2 PM? I can show you her favorite hiding spots and treats. She can be a bit shy at first.

MAN: Perfect! And don't worry about rushing back - I'm happy to watch her for extra days if your plans change.

WOMAN: That's so kind of you! I'll pay you, of course. What's your usual rate for pet-sitting?

MAN: Oh, no need to pay! We're neighbors, and I'm happy to help. Plus, it'll be nice to have a cat around for a change.

WOMAN: Are you sure? At least let me bring you back something nice from my trip as a thank you.

MAN: Well, I wouldn't say no to that! Looking forward to meeting Mittens tomorrow.

## Exam 28 — Part 3: Municipal Waste Collection

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
You will hear a conversation between a resident and a municipal waste management representative.

### Audio Transcript
WOMAN: Good morning, Municipal Waste Management Office. How may I assist you today?

MAN: Hi, I received a notice about changes to our recycling program and collection schedule, but I'm a bit confused about the new system.

WOMAN: I'd be happy to explain the changes. Which neighborhood are you in?

MAN: I'm in the Riverside district, on Cedar Avenue.

WOMAN: Perfect. Starting next month, we're implementing a new three-stream waste system in your area. This means separating your waste into organics, recyclables, and general waste.

MAN: That's different from our current two-bin system. Will we be getting new bins?

WOMAN: Yes, the city will provide each household with a green bin for organic waste. You can continue using your existing blue bin for recyclables and grey bin for general waste. The green bins will be delivered next week.

MAN: I see. And what about the collection schedule? Will it still be weekly?

WOMAN: Actually, that's changing too. Organic waste will be collected weekly, but recyclables and general waste will alternate every other week. So one week we'll collect organics and recyclables, and the next week will be organics and general waste.

MAN: That sounds complicated. How will we know which bins to put out?

WOMAN: We're providing everyone with a color-coded calendar, and you can also download our new mobile app that sends reminders the night before collection day. The app will tell you exactly which bins to put out.

MAN: That's helpful. What exactly goes in the green bin? Just food scraps?

WOMAN: Food scraps, yes, but also yard waste, paper towels, napkins, and even pizza boxes. The only things to avoid are plastic bags, metal, glass, and pet waste. Those go in your general waste bin.

MAN: And what time should we put the bins out?

WOMAN: Bins should be at the curb by 7:00 AM on collection day, but not earlier than 6:00 PM the evening before. Also, please make sure there's at least one foot of space between each bin for our automated collection trucks.

MAN: One more question - what happens during holidays?

WOMAN: If your collection day falls on a holiday, it will be pushed back by one day for the remainder of that week. The app will automatically adjust the schedule and notify you of any changes.

MAN: Great, thanks for explaining everything. I'll download the app right away.

## Exam 28 — Part 5: Library Digital Media

### Prompt / Passage / Instructions
